#2106. Arsenal transfer interest faces major obstacle as Santos secure £83m teenage talent

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal may have to rethink their interest in Santos forward Ignacio Pereira after the Brazilian club secured the teenager’s future with a substantial release clause.

The 16-year-old has caught the eye of a number of European clubs after an impressive campaign in Santos’ youth teams. The likes of Arsenal are said to have been watching his progress.

However, Santos have acted swiftly to secure the services of one of their most exciting young talents. Pereira signed his first professional contract with the club on November 4, tying him to the club until December 2029.

The deal also includes a 100 million euro release clause (around £83.4 million), according to Brazilian journalist Bruno Lima from UOL.

This poses a major problem for Arsenal if they are looking to sign the Argentine but also offers a lot of security for Santos, as they want to develop him as a first-team player.

Pereira has signed a new deal amid increasing interest in his development. Reports in Brazil have previously said that Arsenal, Real Betis, AC Milan, Lille, Standard Liège and Zenit are all keeping an eye on the rising star.

The club have now secured his services for another three years. The new agreement was awaiting registration with the Brazilian Football Confederation when the details emerged.

Pereira has spent three years at Santos, having joined from Juventude in 2023. He previously developed at Grêmio before moving to the São Paulo club.

Pereira has certainly lived up to the expectations. He scored an impressive 6 goals in 17 games in the Brazilian Under-17 Championship, making him the second-highest scorer for Santos. He also scored 4 goals in the Paulista Under-17 Championship.

This is very promising. It is his first season playing at under-17 level.

Pereira has been compared to Julián Álvarez due to his mobility and ability to play outside the box.

But the youngster cites another big name up front as his main inspiration. According to UOL, he cites Manchester City’s Erling Haaland as his inspiration, while Lionel Messi is still his football idol.

His profile suggests a versatile number nine who can play lower down the pitch, be an attacking midfielder and play with another striker. He has impressed the youth coaches at Santos with his finishing ability, physicality and desire to win.

He has a long way to go. Reports from Brazil suggest that Santos want to improve his tactical awareness and behaviour before making him more responsible.

He is being considered by the club for inclusion in their squad for the 2027 Copa São Paulo de Futebol Júnior (known as Copinha) and could start on the bench.

This interest from Arsenal does not necessarily mean that there is an imminent move for Pereira. The player is only 16, and a potential deal is made much more complicated due to a new contract.

Maybe the best course of action for Mikel Arteta’s recruitment team is to keep an eye on him. Santos has made it clear where they stand, and Pereira can now work towards his dream. Being in their first team.

#2105. Opposition insight for Milan-Ferencvaros: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

On Thursday evening, Ferencvaros will travel to San Siro to face AC Milan in the Europa League, in a must-win game for the Rossoneri.

It’s already at that stage for Milan; if they want to qualify for the Round of 16 automatically, they must beat everyone in front of them. With three points from nine available, Ruben Amorim expressed his frustrations with this season so far, and they need to prove themselves tomorrow.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

➤ Manager: Balazs Borbely ➤ Form (all comps): D-W-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Europa League): Kristoffer Zachariassen – 5 ➤ Most assists (Europa League): Yusuf Bamidele & Veljko Birmančević – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bero, Otvos.

Ferencvaros went into last season as defending league champions under head coach Robbie Keane, but were forced to settle for second place. They did win the domestic cup though, and got to the last-16 of the Europa League before being beaten by Braga.

Keane left before the 2026-27 campaign, and he was replaced by Balazs Borbely who came from Gyor ETO, the club that have been one of the surprise packages in recent years, even winning the Nemzeti Bajnokság I (league title) last season.

It was quite a quiet summer for the Budapest-based team, as their big splash was Veljko Birmancevic from Sparta Praha for €2m. Matus Bero and Nathan Zohore arrived on free transfers, while Adam Nagy joined for a low fee from Spezia.

There were a few more exits though: Elton Acolatse, Zsombor Gruber, Mohammed Abu Fani, Gabi Kanichowsky and Cebrail Makreckis all left for figures between €2.5m and €1m, while five departed on free transfers too.

It has been a good start for Borbely, given that Ferencvaros are undefeated in their last 20 matches across all competitions, and they are dreaming of securing direct qualification to the last-16 of the competition.

The Zöldek have three wins from three, occupying fourth place in the overall standings behind Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Bournemouth. To qualify for the group stage, they overcame Twente, Gornik Zabrze and Trabzonspor, beating the latter 5-0 on aggregate.

An away win against Celtic kicked off their league phase, following by victories against Viktoria Plzen and Torreense. Overall, the Hungarian outfit have scored nine times and have conceded just three in what has been a perfect start in the UEL.

Ferencvaros’ only defeat came in their league debut on July 26 (2-4 against Baksi FC). Since then, they have gone on a long unbeaten streak of five wins and five draws, climbing to third place, just two points behind league leaders Gyor and with a game in hand.

In terms of injury news, the visitors will be missing Slovakian midfielder Matus Bero, while Bence Otvos is recovering from an ACL injury and will not take part. Aside from that, they have a clean bill of health.

Borbely’s side have so far alternated between a 4-1-4-1 formation – deploying former Liverpool player Nabi Keita or Adamy Nagy (who played for Bologna and Spezia) as midfielders – and a 4-2-3-1 to offer a bit more width.

A few rotations are expected from the weekend’s game – where they cruised to a 2-0 win – and the first set comes in defence. Radnoti, Nagy, Zohore and O’Dowda are all expected to return to the starting XI, with Gomez being the only survivor to retain his place.

Maiga will find a new partner at the base of the midfield in the aforementioned Nagy, whilst Zachariassen will start ahead of them.

On the wings, it’s an unchanged set-up with leading goalscorer Zachariassen and Birmancevic starting. Then, Yusuf is expected to return to the starting XI.

Predicted Ferencvaros XI (4-2-3-1): Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O’Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf.

Predicted bench: A Varga, Dibusz, Osvath, Raemaekers, Cadu, Madrasz, Corbu, Bamidele, Bero, Joseph, Levi, Arzani, Rommens, Pappoe, Z Varga, Keita.

#2104. Arsenal handed William Saliba boost as Arteta considers defender’s return

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

The William Saliba Arsenal boost comes at a crucial time. Saliba can use the November international break to build up his fitness after missing out on France’s latest squad.

Arteta confirmed that the defender had returned to full training ahead of Arsenal’s Champions League meeting with Slavia Prague. He also completed 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors-friendly last week as he stepped up his recovery.

However, Saliba did not feature in the 2-1 victory. Arteta included him in the matchday squad for the first time this season, but the Frenchman remained an unused substitute.

It means he was not selected by Zinedine Zidane for France’s Nations League games against Italy and Turkey. This gives Arsenal a chance to continue working on his recovery. He will not be travelling for international games or playing in competitive matches.

Saliba has not featured since he suffered a back injury during France’s World Cup semi-final against Spain in July. Arteta has had to find alternatives in central defence in the early stages of the campaign.

Since transferring to Arsenal from Aston Villa in August, Konsa has played a part in filling the gap left by Saliba. His presence in the centre of defence complements Gabriel Magalhães and gives Arteta more options.

The England defender is also expected to be fit for the match against Hull City on Saturday. According to Arteta, the player’s replacement in the game against Slavia Prague was just a precaution after he reported some discomfort.

The fact that he has made a recovery means that Arsenal have the option to control how Saliba returns. Arteta has the possibility of bringing Saliba back gradually, as Konsa is ready to play and Mosquera is also available.

But Saliba’s return still matters. He needs to get back in shape before the fixtures start getting tougher after the international break.

Arteta has made it clear he will respect whatever decision Zidane makes regarding Saliba’s availability but acknowledges that he needs some game time after being out for so long.

France will play Italy on November 12 and then Turkey three days later. This means Saliba will be missing those matches, as Zidane named his 23-man squad on Friday.

This means he will be able to continue to be monitored by the club at their London Colney training ground. He won’t be able to return to play in international games ahead of his first appearance for the club.

Arsenal will be hoping that he can use the extra time to get himself ready for the next set of games, including a trip to Newcastle before playing Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City at home.

Arteta will be keen to have Saliba back in contention but will be focused on getting him back at the right time.

There is some immediate optimism on Konsa’s fitness for the game against Hull. But more importantly, Saliba has now progressed to a point where he can be included in the planning process.

#2103. Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal set January transfer priorities as Fabrizio Romano delivers Piero Hincapié update

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal transfer news, Arsenal could approach the January transfer window with a different focus after Fabrizio Romano revealed that Mikel Arteta has no intention of weakening his defensive options.

Piero Hincapié has been linked with a move to Barcelona. There have been reports that a deal could be done involving Alejandro Balde, but Romano expects the Ecuadorian to stay at Emirates Stadium.

Arsenal have been strengthening their defensive department under Arteta. Hincapié only made the switch permanently from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer after joining on loan.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

However, Arsenal have little incentive to let him leave halfway through the season, as losing a two-in-one defender will cause problems for Arteta, given how much they need to do in multiple competitions.

Romano’s comments suggest that Arsenal are happy with their existing defensive unit and don’t want to cause any disruption to their balance. He also suggested that Hincapié is an important player for them, meaning he’s unlikely to leave in January.

That leaves Barcelona needing to explore alternative targets if they want to strengthen their backline. A deal involving Balde and Hincapié does not currently appear to be a realistic option.

The more interesting part of Romano’s report is Arsenal’s potential business at the other end of the field.

He feels they will be looking to make a move if the right attacking player comes up for grabs. But he doesn’t think they will make a signing just because they can in January.

This highlights the issues clubs face with mid-season transfers. Often selling clubs will be unwilling to lose key players, and finding suitable replacements can be tough.

As such, Arsenal are likely to look at the market to see what they can do. However, it looks like there could still be a forward brought in.

This is an important distinction. The point being made here is that whilst there is speculation around one particular player, Romano has indicated that Arsenal can strengthen their attacking options. This is not to say that any particular move is happening.

If Arteta keeps Hincapié, then Arsenal will maintain their defensive stability and possibly gain another option in attack.

Over the next few weeks we will get a better understanding of what is available to them. But for now it looks like Arsenal are not keen to lose Hincapié but will look to strengthen their attacking options if the right deal comes along.

#2102. Arsenal vs Hull City preview: Arteta sticks with winning formula as Gunners target another three points

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have resisted the temptation to rotate after their victory at Anfield, with Mikel Arteta naming the same starting XI for Saturday’s meeting with Hull City.

Arsenal welcome Championship side Hull City to the Emirates Stadium, looking to strengthen their grip on the top spot after collecting 24 points from their opening nine Premier League games. However, their tally of just 14 goals suggests Arteta’s side still have work to do in the final third.

Arteta has again chosen to partner Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães in defence. William Saliba was left out despite pre-match talk that he would be named in the starting XI. Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman are also missing from the squad.

Noni Madueke will carry the right. Tzolis starts on the opposite flank. Kai Havertz will lead the line. Viktor Gyökeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino add attacking options from the bench.

Arsenal predicted starting XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice, Ødegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

Substitutes: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Hincapié, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Gyökeres.

Hull are coming into this game ranked 11th in the league after five draws in their first nine games. They’ve not won in their last eight games but can cause problems for any opposition.

They look like playing a defensive game with Slater, Iroegbunam and Gourna-Douath in the midfield to protect the backline. McBurnie and Cho will give them some attacking options.

Hull starting XI: Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud; Slater, Iroegbunam, Gourna-Douath; McBurnie, Cho.

Substitutes: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Mouzakitis, Vaz.

McBurnie is just one booking away from suspension for the clash against Brighton on November 22 but may make an important impact in the physical battle with Gabriel.

Hull have not scored at the Emirates since 2014 but will look to turn that around. However, their main concern will be to ensure they keep Arsenal quiet for as long as possible.

Arsenal will need to find ways to break down the likely tight Hull backline.

Ødegaard and Rice will be key in keeping possession and creating chances, whilst Madueke and Tzolis will create width and movement.

Hull may be exposed to threat in case they are trapped in defence for too long, but Arteta can use Gyökeres if Havertz is having difficulties doing anything productive.

A win for Arsenal will give them a six-point lead. Manchester City will be looking to get all three points when they face Nottingham Forest later on Saturday.

The visitors will look to create an uncomfortable afternoon for the Gunners.

Arsenal have enough quality to take all three points, but Hull will not make it easy for them. I expect this to be a tight game, and the Gunners will win by a small margin.

#2100. Arsenal 1-0 Hull City: Martin Ødegaard rescues Gunners with late winner at the Emirates

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal needed a moment of quality from their captain to overcome Hull City and claim a narrow 1-0 Premier League victory at the Emirates Stadium.

Martin Ødegaard scored in the 72nd minute as the hosts struggled to break down a resolute Hull side. It was much like I expected in my match preview, as Arsenal had to work hard to win this game.

The result gives them an extended lead at the top of the table. Ahead of Manchester City’s clash with Nottingham Forest. However, Mikel Arteta will be aware that his team did not play well in this game. It was far from a walk in the park.

Hull arrived at London looking to play an attacking game. Jakirovic’s side were well organised and looked to launch quick counter attacks.

They did have some positive moments in the first half, but Arsenal struggled to get into their attacking rhythm. Kai Havertz couldn’t capitalise on one good chance created by Ødegaard.

The hosts were hopeful of taking the lead after Havertz fell to the ground in the box after being pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

However, referee Farai Hallam’s initial decision was overturned after a VAR review showed Havertz was offside earlier in the attack, so Arsenal’s penalty was cancelled.

Another frustrating moment for the home side, who failed to score during the first half, despite dominating possession.

Arsenal came out strong after the break. However, Hull were still causing problems. Lewie Coyle was also walking a fine line after a yellow card in the first half and a late challenge on Christos Tzolis.

Arteta made a three-man change on the hour mark, bringing on Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino for Havertz and Declan Rice. Six minutes later he brought on Eberechi Eze and Piero Hincapié.

The breakthrough came from Madueke, forcing Konstantinos Tzolakis into action. The Hull keeper couldn’t hold his shot, and Ødegaard was quickest to react, scoring from the rebound.

The captain’s strike took the frustration out of Arsenal’s efforts and was a reward for their perseverance. It also provided another vital moment for the Norwegian. He’s had a tough campaign so far due to injuries.

Despite going behind, Hull never gave up in their search for an equaliser. However, Arsenal held on to their lead.

Arsenal dominated the game with 67% of possession and 21 shots, compared to just seven for Hull. Tzolakis put in a number of key interventions to keep the scoreline respectable.

Although they weren’t at their best, Arsenal were able to perform in the key moments of the game. Ødegaard’s goal meant that the Gunners earned three points and are sitting top of the Premier League heading into the international break.

#2097. Romano assesses ‘perfect’ derby win, the restart and Milan’s mercato targets: “A busy January”

Today, Fabrizio Romano has taken an in-depth look at AC Milan, their big weekend result and what’s next for the club.

After the Derby della Madonnina, there’s a very strong feeling surrounding Milan. All of a sudden, talk of winning a Scudetto under Ruben Amorim has gained genuine traction, and the group looks closer than ever.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s not going to be easy, of course, but the Portuguese is obsessed with the idea of lifting the Serie A trophy with the Rossoneri, referencing as much in his press conference earlier today.

If that is going to happen this season, though, they will need to invest in January. After all, the squad remains shallow and extra support is very much needed.

Speaking to Time2Play.com, Romano looked at several things, including the derby and what the next few months could look like for the Diavolo.

“A derby can change the world. Because often, dynamics are triggered on and off the pitch, the atmosphere clears in an instant, and everyone contributes.

“AC Milan knows this well: a week ago, the home defeat against Bologna had brought much criticism, though it was also clearly the result of fatigue and significant absences, given the relentless pace of matches.

“But immediately afterwards, AC Milan set up their perfect derby—on and off the pitch, it’s no small matter—to build on and not just sit back.

“Because on the pitch, from Moreira to the usual Rabiot and Ruben Amorim, defended tooth and nail by Cardinale, everyone contributed that touch that led to the three points with a ferocious approach that became a winner.

“Off the pitch, Gerry Cardinale himself left his mark. Never like this.”

“The induction of legends during the week, Ricardo Kaká in the Hall of Fame, the announcement of the new stadium alongside Inter, interviews to staunchly defend Ruben Amorim, and above all, the desire to continue improving his AC Milan 2.0 starting… in January.

“Yes, because the Rossoneri’s post-derby signals are about building, not just about exaltation. This is where we need to start again, laying the foundations for a different, fierce, and winning Milan, like the one seen in the derby, which clearly can’t be enough.”

“And the first announcement will be that of the new Head of Football: Milan has a sealed verbal agreement with Markus Krösche, the man who has done a great job at Eintracht Frankfurt in recent years, both in scouting talent and capital gains, ready to take over the Rossoneri project.

“Krösche will be active for the January transfer window and will be in direct contact with Cardinale regarding the Rossoneri’s new plans.

“He’s a figure generating enthusiasm at Casa Milan, having already been the first choice since last June: Cardinale preferred to wait a few months to have his priority rather than fall back on managers who weren’t first choices. Now, the Krösche era is about to begin.”

“Milan’s objectives? It’s going to be a busy January: the defender could and should have arrived at the end of August, but there was no timeline or method. Milan has reinstated Tomori, but at least one defensive reinforcement is already planned for January.

“The favourite since June has been Sporting’s Gonçalo Inacio, but Milan has at least three other options on the list and has recently also sent Sylla of Union St. Gilloise to scout. It might not end there: keep an eye on the attack, where an additional option to give Gonçalo Ramos a rest shouldn’t be ruled out if the right opportunity presents itself.

“Assessments about Franceso Camarda will be made in the coming weeks, but Milan is exploring the transfer market and will continue to surprise. At least one signing, likely two. And then… the transfer market will dictate inspiration, ideas, and innovations.

“With new players and a Rossoneri that has never been so fired up in recent years.”

For the first time in a while, it’s a continued stream of positive news for Milan, which is only a good thing.

Jacob Murphy with a superb left foot long range strike that looked to have won it on 80 minutes, only for Fulham to hit back with an equaliser three minutes later as United failed to clear their lines and a couple of deflections aided Fulham.

Referee Rob Jones was woeful as usual with Newcastle United, looking to give Fulham as many decisions as possible.

Four games in London for Matthias Jaissle in all competitions and still unbeaten, three wins and a draw in the capital.

#2094. Is one point away from home ever a bad point? Fulham 1 Newcastle 1

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

In answer to the question above, the outcome at Craven Cottage definitely felt as if Newcastle United had dropped two rather than gained one, perhaps because we conceded a late equaliser.

Compared with May’s encounter, in what proved to be Eddie Howe’s final Premier League game as our head coach, the performance was much better, though still a long way below what I believe is possible.

Before kick-off I would have taken the draw. I said as much to a Fulham fan on the walk from Putney Bridge Tube station through Bishops Park. An American, she lives in Clapham and last season needed to choose a London club to support when her most recent serious relationship ended. No way would she continue to cheer for his team!

Her choice of Fulham was based partly on the club’s questionable claim to be the oldest in the capital. When I pointed out that in 147 years Fulham had never won a big trophy (domestic or European) she replied that she followed football for the fun, not the glory. An admirable attitude . . .

We shook hands and wished each other good luck at 2.30pm on the corner of the Riverside and Putney End stands. Another random conversation to add to the collection.

On the train up from Brighton I had quizzed an Arsenal fan, who was taking his two sons to The Emirates for the game against Hull.

What was his verdict on Bruno G? Why wasn’t our former captain a regular starter?

“We rotate nearly every match. Arteta picks him against teams who play a low block. I like Bruno because he’s always looking forward, trying to create. Lewis-Skelly is preferred in European games, which are more open. We also have Eze, who is probably 13th on the team sheet.”

A veritable wealth of riches for the title-winning manager.

Not that the Arsenal fan on the train had been confident last season, fearing the recent history of blowing their chances was likely to be repeated again.

Hadn’t Arsenal succeeded at last despite Arteta, rather than because of him, I suggested. The style of football was efficient rather than attractive. When we went to The Emirates in April, with Man City hot on Arsenal’s heels, the tension was palpable. An Eze cracker from a short corner routine saw them home that day. Another 1-0 to The Arsenal, just as they managed yesterday against Hull City.

How will they cope against Newcastle 2.0, when they meet at St James’ Park immediately after the international break? If United play to their full potential, with Sean Steur making things tick in midfield and Lewis Hall surging up the wing after quelling attacks, anything is possible. We proved that in the 2024/25 season, when we beat them three times.

Possible but unlikely, because we no longer have Isak and Gordon to fire the bullets supplied by Bruno G. Neither do we have the oh-so-predictable leadership of Howe; predictable as in getting the better of Arteta with pleasing frequency.

We lacked that sort of firepower yesterday. William Osula ran relentlessly to little effect. Yoane Wissa rarely showed the same enthusiasm. The chemistry between them looked embryonic, being charitable. The link play between Amar Dedic and Jacob Murphy on the right flank, between Hall and Harvey Barnes on the left, was sporadic to nonexistent.

When the full-backs advanced, the wide attackers dropped back. That was an understandable response to conceding three goals at Everton, four at Coventry and four at Leeds since mid-September. One consequence was a lot of sideways and backward passing, to the travelling fans’ frustration.

Another consequence was the need for Murphy and Barnes to defend if Fulham regained possession, which they did reasonably well.

With Steur and Nico Gonzalez in the middle of the park, supplemented by their wider teammates, United looked less open.

Matthias Jaissle has been widely blamed for trying to succeed with a two-man midfield. Yesterday the two was often a four, thanks to Dedic and Hall stepping up while Murphy and Barnes stepped back.

Total football it was not. It was, however, more encouraging than a lot of what we have seen in the German’s first three months in charge.

Dan Burn defended solidly and strode forward more than once, trying to make things happen. Malick Thiaw blocked and intercepted impressively from first to last, though his passing was occasionally alarming.

In the interests of research I watched the Everton v Coventry televised game on Friday evening. The referee at the Hill Dickinson was the biggest Homer since Ancient Greece, denying the visitors two penalties and ignoring a handball in Everton’s second goal. VAR refused to get involved just as Howard Webb, head of Pro Ref, wants.

I feared more of the same at Craven Cottage. Rob Jones didn’t disappoint. He was biased with a capital B, favouring the hosts whenever there was an element of doubt and often when there wasn’t. Fouls on visiting players went unpunished, whereas strong challenges by United were often penalised.

The first half contained only a few glimpses of fluid passing from either team. Lukas Hornicek made a couple of spectacular saves, while Barnes forced Bernd Leno to kick away a clever flick from a low Murphy cross. The Fulham keeper also stopped a goal-bound Barnes shot, this time unwittingly with his forehead.

Burn finished smartly at the near post from the resultant corner but the referee deemed Wissa had fouled Timothy Castagne with the sort of routine holding that is usually ignored by the officials.

After the interval United looked more dangerous as they attacked the Putney End that housed the vociferous Toon Army. Barnes cracked a right-foot curler off the outside of the post with Leno nowhere, Wissa was maybe two feet short of a tap-in from another low cross and for a few minutes Fulham struggled to break out of their half.

The replacement of Gonzalez and Wissa by Lewis Miley and Joe Willock on 61 minutes added to the threat. Steur was always available and kept the ball moving in midfield but struggled to recover from a heavy tackle. He made way for Matias Fernandez-Pardo, whose pace immediately unsettled Fulham.

When Murphy seized on a loose pass about 40 yards out on our right flank, he jinked inside, set his sights and with his left boot bent a sizzling shot beyond Leno. Mayhem among the travelling fans!

The cheers and chants were still bouncing around the stadium three minutes later when the equaliser went in. It has been credited to Rodrigo Muniz. Having watched the goal six times on television replays, I reckon Hall kicked the ball onto the Brazilian before it deflected off the diving Burn and into the net past a wrong-footed Hornicek. Perhaps a trip to Specsavers is needed . . .

Neither team were happy to settle for a point. A rapid break down the left led to Hall finding space 12 yards out. Sadly for him and his team, the ball was on his weaker boot and Leno was able to save the low shot.

Fulham could have stolen all three points in stoppage time when Ryan Sessegnon smashed a 20-yarder to Hornicek’s left. The young keeper dived across and parried it to safety, capping what was probably his best game so far for United.

One point gained or two dropped? I favour the latter verdict. We had the better chances in a tight game and should have taken three of them.

Newcastle are a work in progress. There’s plenty of room for improvement but there were enough signs yesterday to suggest we’re heading in the right direction.

Fulham 1 Newcastle United 1 – Saturday 7 November 2026 3pm

Shots on target were Newcastle 5 Fulham 5

Touches in the opposition box Newcastle 19 Fulham 27

Hornicek, Dedic, Thiaw (Schar 85), Burn, Hall, Gonzalez (Miley 61), Steur (Fernanez-Pardo 74), Barnes, Wissa (Willock 61), Murphy, Osula (Elanga 85)

#2093. Europa League preview: AC Milan vs. Ferencvaros – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

AC Milan are back in front of their own fans on Thursday night, hoping to correct their European course against Ferencvaros.

Milan are buoyed by the derby win over Inter at the weekend, and yet in continental competition they have struggled so far having lost two of three. So, the pressure remains on to bounce back and start climbing the Europa League table before it is too late.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In his pre-match press conference, Ruben Amorim admitted that his side needed to find some consistency, especially after the win against Inter. Effectively, his message was that the win would mean little if it wasn’t followed with another three points.

Game date: Thursday, November 4 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Urs Schnyder (VAR: Fähndrich)

As mentioned above, Milan could hardly be going into this game feeling any better after they scored three first-half goals to down their city rivals for a fourth straight time. Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira scored in a 3-1 win that was well engineered by Ruben Amorim.

The Rossoneri continue to demonstrate their potential domestically, even if they remain seven points off top, but in the Europa League things haven’t gone to plan. Losses to Benfica and Bournemouth – both without scoring – either side of the rout of RB Salzburg leave them on three points from three games.

That puts Milan in 24th place in the table on goals scored, which is the final play-off spot. So, a big improvement is needed in the final five games of the league phase in order for the tag of being among the pre-tournament favourites to be justified.

Mario Gila, Rabiot and Moreira all returned to the line-up against Inter, which provided a very noticeable boost. However, there are no new recoveries in view of the match against Ferencvaros, so the depth is still limited.

Fikayo Tomori is in the treatment room after suffering a torn muscle in his right thigh, joining Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze who also remain out. The latter may yet require surgery on a hip issue.

The other major absentee is Mike Maignan, who saw red for shoving Tyler Adams in the face during the last Europa League game against Bournemouth and will be forced to serve a one-match ban, which is less than feared.

The latest from the various media reports suggests that Amorim will field quite a youthful side, as he has done in Europe so far. This means chances should be given to Lorenzo Torriani, Sankhoun Diawara, Ardon Jashari, Davide Bartesaghi, Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse and potentially more.

Expectations about rotation seem likely to be proven right, with the defence being almost completely changed. Without a back-up, Torriani is indeed given the nod.

Then, the backline is made of a largely rotated group. Filippo Terracciano will start at right-back, whilst Koni De Winter will partner Diawara in the middle of the back four. Bartesaghi returns at left-back.

In midfield, Hutchinson and Cisse will start on the flanks as expected, with Yunus Musah and Jashari given the nod in the middle of the park.

Despite suggestions that Camarda could start, it seems Goncalo Ramos will be given the starting role again.

Predicted Milan XI (4-4-1-1): Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Cisse; Rabiot; Ramos

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Comotto, Modric, Moreira, Pulisic, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Maignan, Pavlovic, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze, Gabbia, Tomori, Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano.

Ferencvaros went into last season as defending league champions under head coach Robbie Keane, but were forced to settle for second place. They did win the domestic cup though, and got to the last-16 of the Europa League before being beaten by Braga.

Keane left before the 2026-27 campaign, and he was replaced by Balazs Borbely who came from Gyor ETO, the club that have been one of the surprise packages in recent years, even winning the Nemzeti Bajnokság I (league title) last season.

It was quite a quiet summer for the Budapest-based team, as their big splash was Veljko Birmancevic from Sparta Praha for €2m. Matus Bero and Nathan Zohore arrived on free transfers, while Adam Nagy joined for a low fee from Spezia.

There were a few more exits though: Elton Acolatse, Zsombor Gruber, Mohammed Abu Fani, Gabi Kanichowsky and Cebrail Makreckis all left for figures between €2.5m and €1m, while five departed on free transfers too.

It has been a good start for Borbely, given that Ferencvaros are undefeated in their last 20 matches across all competitions, and they are dreaming of securing direct qualification to the last-16 of the competition.

The Zöldek have three wins from three, occupying fourth place in the overall standings behind Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Bournemouth. To qualify for the group stage, they overcame Twente, Gornik Zabrze and Trabzonspor, beating the latter 5-0 on aggregate.

An away win against Celtic kicked off their league phase, following by victories against Viktoria Plzen and Torreense. Overall, the Hungarian outfit have scored nine times and have conceded just three in what has been a perfect start in the UEL.

Ferencvaros’ only defeat came in their league debut on July 26 (2-4 against Baksi FC). Since then, they have gone on a long unbeaten streak of five wins and five draws, climbing to third place, just two points behind league leaders Gyor and with a game in hand.

In terms of injury news, the visitors will be missing Slovakian midfielder Matus Bero, while Bence Otvos is recovering from an ACL injury and will not take part. Aside from that, they have a clean bill of health.

Borbely’s side have so far alternated between a 4-1-4-1 formation – deploying former Liverpool player Nabi Keita or Adamy Nagy (who played for Bologna and Spezia) as midfielders – and a 4-2-3-1 to offer a bit more width.

A few rotations are expected from the weekend’s game – where they cruised to a 2-0 win – and the first set comes in defence. Radnoti, Nagy, Zohore and O’Dowda are all expected to return to the starting XI, with Gomez being the only survivor to retain his place.

Maiga will find a new partner at the base of the midfield in the aforementioned Nagy, whilst Zachariassen will start ahead of them.

On the wings, it’s an unchanged set-up with leading goalscorer Zachariassen and Birmancevic starting. Then, Yusuf is expected to return to the starting XI.

Predicted Ferencvaros XI (4-2-3-1): Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O’Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf.

Predicted bench: A Varga, Dibusz, Osvath, Raemaekers, Cadu, Madrasz, Corbu, Bamidele, Bero, Joseph, Levi, Arzani, Rommens, Pappoe, Z Varga, Keita.

This will be the first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros, making it a historic encounter as a result.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match. Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencáros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026/2027.

➤ AC Milan will look to build on their derby success when they welcome an unbeaten Ferencváros side to the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday evening. Ruben Amorim’s team have enjoyed a promising domestic campaign but struggled to replicate that form in Europe, occupying 24th place in the league-phase standings with just three points from their opening three matches. Their Hungarian opponents, meanwhile, sit fourth with a perfect nine-point return and arrive in Italy chasing a fourth consecutive European victory.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter Milan at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing. They suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11. Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures. Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967/68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level. Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

Sankhoun Diawara has been superb so far when called upon, and he’ll replace the ever-present Strahinja Pavlovic here. A big performance would not only reassure the club of his ability (and potential), but it may offer a reason to change January plans.

It feels like a weekly occurrence now, but Goncalo Ramos needs a goal. If Francesco Camarda is not going to start here, the Portuguese needs to prove that there is reason to keep the youngster on the bench. For his sake, as much as the Italian’s.

For the visitors, Kristoffer Zachariassen is the main danger man. Contributing to 11 goals in 21 games so far this season, the 32-year-old will be essential to Ferencvaros getting anything on Thursday.

Then, Mariano Gomez will represent a difficult opponent for whoever leads the Rossoneri’s line. The Argentine defender has been excellent so far this season, and it’s entirely possible that he contributes to a frustrating night.

Despite their rotations, Milan must win here; if they don’t, they’ll wave their Europa League top eight wishes goodbye. There’s enough quality in the starting XI to provide three points, so that will be the expectation.

AWAY from the training pitch and from all things Scott Parker for a second, with a change of focus to events within the board room and at the helm of West Ham United. Kretinsky – fully involved, according to our source, along with the CEO in the behind the scenes running of the football club

“Acting Chief Exec Karim Virani now fully immersed in the day to day running of the club and now liasing with major shareholder Daniel Kretinsky on relevant matters”.

Virani, whilst still ‘acting’ CEO’ by title, appears now very much immersed in the leadership of the club and was, according to Jacob Steinberg, involved along with Nils Koppen in the decision to part company with Nuno Espírito Santo – not before time.

#2091. ‘Painful’ – Alexis Mac Allister doesn’t hold back about ‘unpleasant situation’ at Liverpool

Alexis Mac Allister has spoken out about his ‘painful, unpleasant situation’ at Liverpool in terms of not being offered a new contract.

The Argentine caused a stir in September when he said that he was ‘very sad‘ not to have been offered a new deal by the club, having seen fellow 2023 signings Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai both pen contract extensions earlier this year.

The Telegraph’s Dominic King reported last month that Anfield chiefs aren’t in ‘any rush’ to begin talks over a new deal for the Reds’ number 10 (who’s contracted to June 2028), despite his resurgence in form since the start of this season.

Appearing on the Los Edul show in his homeland, Mac Allister spoke candidly about Liverpool’s decision not to offer him new terms over the past few months.

The 27-year-old said: “We’re in a situation where I have a year and a half left on my contract. Last season I was told that the club’s idea was not to renew it, at least for now, and obviously that was a painful, unpleasant situation.”

When asked if the situation was making him despondent, he replied: “Not that much, because at the end of the day, I still had – and still have – time left at this club, which is what I want most – to stay here.

“The reality is that the manager has now changed, the sporting director has changed, and new investors are coming into the club, so I think I’m now in a position where anything can happen. We’ll see what happens in the future. I’ve always said that I’m very happy here, that I really enjoy it, and we’ll see.”

Mac Allister added: “Look at Szoboszlai and Gravenberch. They’re two players who were in the same contractual situation as me, and when I was told that, they renewed their contracts.

“It was more a position taken by the club, and generally that’s how things are done. At the end of the day, as a club you don’t want to lose a lot of money, and you don’t want players leaving on free transfers either.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

That the Argentine has spoken out publicly about his contract situation once more gives a strong hint that privately he’s seething at not being offered a new deal in the same way that Szoboszlai and Gravenberch were.

Admittedly Mac Allister’s collapse in form last season may have triggered a reluctance from the club to commit to a contract extension for a player who’ll be 29 when his current terms expire, and he’s a bit older than his aforementioned midfield teammates.

However, the ex-Brighton man has been excellent in the first two months of this campaign, almost as though he’s motivated by a burning desire to earn a new deal at Anfield and show that the hierarchy have been mistaken in their reluctance to tie him down for the long-term.

The 2022 World Cup winner is currently on £180,000 per week at Liverpool, a figure exceeded by 10 of his teammates (Capology), and it could be the case that he’s seeking a higher amount than what the club are prepared to offer him.

Mac Allister could hardly have made his desire for a new contract any clearer. We don’t know exactly why his situation is taking longer to resolve than those of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch, but if he keeps performing on the pitch, then surely it’s just a matter of when and not if he’s offered an extension by the Anfield hierarchy.

#2089. Fulham 1 Newcastle 1 match ratings and comments on all Newcastle United players

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

We asked Dave Marshall to give us his match ratings and comments on individual Newcastle United players after Fulham 1 Newcastle 1.

Nail-biting. Teeth gnashing. Unease. Anxiety. Growing disapproval. Such were the rumblings of a sizable, and growing, section of Newcastle supporters as United headed to west London for a date with Fulham.

The Cottagers a side going in just two points above relegation but showing signs of life in recent weeks.

A good omen for United going in, though: winning three on the bounce in the capital this season with no goals conceded.

But pressure mounting on Matthias Jaissle and the lads after a string of bad results.

While there are both positives and negatives to take from this performance and result v Fulham…

What’s most concerning is the vibe around the club.

It was noticeable Monday at St. James’ Park. And the ranting and raving online has reached ridiculous levels of theatre.

It was good that Newcastle had an away match after capitulating twice to the Merseyside Mackems because St. James’ Park would have been too toxic to have been any support for the black and white today.

This is not the place to debate Jaissle’s tenure or his seemingly increasingly tenuous position to remain United’s gaffer.

This is not the place to criticise the personnel decisions the brass have made in recent months.

Nor is to call out any players for lack of effort, skill, finishing, passing, common sense, etc.

But it is a place to remind you that we are Newcastle United.

And United supporters have a reputation for being among the most loyal, fervent, rabid, and supportive.

50,000 strong showed up on the regular even when having to endure seasons in the Championship.

Traveling Geordies are always lauded, especially on the continent. It’s no stretch to say that a lot of club brass around England are envious of the support Newcastle gets. Supporters who bleed black-and-white.

Think 50,000 would regularly show up if one of the Septics got relegated after so many years without any trophies and Mike Ashley the club owner?

(It’s still early, but we’re on course to find out next season… but I digress.)

Face it… this is nothing compared to the dark ages of the Fat Tub of Ashley years.

The struggles of a team that lost three of its top skill players and several of its top leaders and mostly replaced them with younger, greener, and arguably less-skilled footballers?

Not the worst times United supporters have ever endured.

The learning curve of a new gaffer who’s not been on the touchline even three months yet?

Not the worst depths Geordies have suffered through.

A string of bad performances, bad results, erratic play, defensive mishaps, poor finishing in front of the net…

Not happy with MJ’s tactics or his line-ups or his substitutions or his in-game management?

But what sucks more is the vibe of the supporters right now.

It’s as if a sizable portion of the fanbase is already certain that Matthias Jaissle is a failure and this team is not worthy of support.

The schedule ramps up in quality and intensity after this international break.

So it’s time for us as United supporters to ramp up our own intensity, passion, love, and support for the black-and-white.

Come matchday, it’s time to strap on our favourite United top and do nothing but get behind the team 100%.

When the season kicked off on August 23 at home to Liverpool, pretty much no one expected United to be on 12 points and hovering mid-table after Matchday 10.

Newcastle were tagged for relegation and left for Championship dead. So it’s fair to say that United have exceeded expectations so far.

It’s also easy to forget during a long season, particularly in the midst of a spell of bad results.

Anfield and Old Trafford get all the plaudits for being difficult venues for opponents.

But those of us who live and breathe English football know, even objectively, that no set of supporters gives its team that vital push more than the rabid throngs inside a pulsating St. James’ Park.

And that’s what we have to be again to get through this.

Lukas Hornicek – 8 Bounced back after the flub v Everton on Monday. Stood tall with five saves, several of them spectacular, including early on to deny Oscar Bobb and then a last-second stop to deny Sessegnon’s laserbolt in stoppage time. Can’t be faulted on the equaliser; nothing to be done once it deflected off BDB.

Amar Dedic – 6.5 While he seemed to handle Iwobi, he struggled with Robinson’s overlapping runs. Solid in the first half as United sat back, but lagged as the match went on, his 92nd-minute yellow card invited unnecessary pressure as the draw played out.

Malick Thiaw – 7 Much-needed athleticism was back on the backline. Composed, accurate for most of his time on the pitch. Didn’t clear the ball well enough in the build up to the equaliser.

Dan Burn – 6.5 Goal disallowed due to a soft foul by Wissa. Dominant in the air, and though unlucky for Muniz’s poke to deflect off him for the equaliser, not quick enough to close down the cross that led to it. Solid partnership with Thiaw.

Lewis Hall – 7 As good as we all think Hall to be, and no doubt we’re correct, to be truly world class, he’s got to bury that 88th-minute effort, even with his non-dominant right foot. Back to his usual level for the most part, otherwise.

Sean Steur – 6.5 Good to see him back and playing with confidence. Was tidy on the ball and always looking to direct passes forward. Still not sure about him being part of a two-man midfield. Not really sure about it generally speaking, to be fair.

Nico Gonzalez – 6 Had his moments in the middle of the park, but wonder about his fitness, as he was subbed for the 2nd game in a row on the hour mark. Though he helped United keep their shape, there was no creativity to his game to break down Fulham’s low block.

Yoane Wissa – 5 Will be aggrieved with the soft foul he got called for that cancelled Burn’s would-be goal. Still, can’t put himself in position for such a call. Had a couple of opportunities but made a meal of them. Didn’t trouble the GK as much as he should have.

Jacob Murphy – 8 A screaming curler that should’ve won it and was denied an assist for Burn’s header. A Murphinho performance that United needs more consistently from him, as he was Newcastle’s most consistent threat on the break.

Harvey Barnes – 6.5 Harsh? Maybe. But when you’re an “all-he-does-is-score” kind of footballer, you’ve got to put away at least one of the three glaring chances he didn’t. He caused Fulham all types of issues but not scoring is unforgivable and it cost United two points.

William Osula – 5 Was not the beneficiary of much good service but his inconsistent effort was disappointing, Did not get a shot on goal.

Lewis Miley – 6 Came on for Nico on 61’, vital defensive header to clear a dangerous Iwobi free-kick late but hope competition with Steur will have him passing more forward. Still, good to see him back.

Joe Willock – 6 On for Wissa on 61’, he added energy dynamism to the midfield but only managed 1 SOG, and it was from long range, not too troublesome.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo – 5 On for Steur on 74’, back for the first time in weeks. Late header was saved but not too much impact. Seemed to suffer a knock in stoppage time, so hope it’s not too serious.

Anthony Elanga – N/A (On too late to rate) On for Osula on 85’, no impact in this cameo.

Fabian Schar – N/A (On too late to rate) On for Thiaw on 85’ following the equaliser to help see things out.

Matthias Jaissle – 6 Not sure that this match set-up worked, not with our cast of characters. However, Jaissle’s plan to sit deep and counter was not a bad idea, given the past couple of weeks. A sniff of desperation? Not sure, but it almost worked perfectly. However, another failure to hold the lead. You can blame MJ all you want, but it was the same last season under Howe, and with a much different cast. It’s hard to explain. But it’s got to be fixed.

Saturday’s Championship tie is the first league meeting of these two sides in fifteen years: The two sides have enjoyed very different histories since the 1 – 1 draw at Ewood Park in 2010. West Ham went on to European triumph in the interim, whilst for tomorrow’s hosts, their relegation from the Premier League in 2011/12 meant they went down as we went up, and the two sides haven’t met since apart from a 5 – 1 West Ham FA Cup victory in 2016.

Last time the two sides met one Mr Dmitri Payet was in full flow

“It’s the one that I’ve been looking forward to, to be honest with you,” Montgomery said.

‘Fourteenth place for a reason’, Blackburn.

Another Saturday afternoon kick-off beckons in this crazy Championship season which offers ‘feast or famine’ football. The second international break kicks in after todays game, with a further maddening two week hiatus after the Hammers’ latest three games in eight days physical assault course.

Surprisingly, only Kyle Walker Peters appears on the ‘injury list’ for West Ham, despite 14 league and 3 cup games already undertaken. Compared with our opponents today who have several players likely out injured, West Ham’s mixture of good luck and good player management seems to be doing the trick again this season, as it did last.

Walker Peters is likely to be the sole enforced absentee in Scott Parker’s match day squad

Speaking ahead of the game, Blackburn Rovers’ veteran coach Tony Mowbray evidently plans to reprise the tactics deployed by Millwall, Southampton, Cardiff and others -and expose West Ham’s well known early defensive frailties:

“”They’re beatable. They’ve lost their manager because they’ve lost too many games this year already and I haven’t seen a team that I think, ‘wow, they’re miles too good for us’.

“Swansea might give that impression, but I think we should be positive, aggressive, play on the front foot and try our hand and see how we get on against West Ham United.” (lancashiretelegraph.co.uk)

West Ham fans will hope to see a more confident, solid foundation created in just a few days – more than Nuno managed to instil in over a year: A tough ask, which is why it may still be far too soon to expect wholesale change.

Scoring the first goal – or two – would prove something of a welcome relief to the 7000 expected Irons fans travelling to the game today, who will all be aware of the Hammers’ terrible propensity to concede first.

As will Parker. Let’s see if he’s managed to instil, at the very least a new combative spirit in his players, and continue on with Wednesday’s second half mentality. Because the Hammers cannot rely on coming back from the dead every week.

#2084. Milan Futuro 2-1 Piacenza: Rossoneri move up to third in Serie D in rescheduled fixture

Today, the Milan Futuro side caught up in the fixture list, with their postponed game against Piacenza, originally scheduled for Matchday 5.

After their win last week, Milan were looking to make it two in a row and four unbeaten today, in the second half of their game against Piacenza, and they did. A 2-1 scoreline, the young Rossoneri have now moved up to third, overtaking today’s opponents.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Casting your minds back to the first half of the game on October 14, the Rossoneri were probably the weaker team. However, it was postponed due to an injury suffered by the referee, Prencipe.

The ‘second half’, then, started strongly for Navarro’s side, as they took the lead within the first five minutes. A well-orchestrated move finished by Lorenzo Ossola, and a brilliant start to the game.

It wasn’t all the Diavolo, though, and the visitors put a lot of pressure on the game, especially on the counter-attack. However, Milan held on and eventually doubled their lead in the 66th minute, thanks to Silvano Vos.

Things almost got nervy when Piacenza got one back from a set-piece, and a tense ending was set up. However, the scoreline remained the same and the Futuro took all three points.

#2083. West Ham winger has to prove the Tottenham doubters wrong – here’s how

West Ham United and Tottenham Hotspur seem to be holding their noses and doing transfer business with each other after a feud between the two club chairmen prohibited any sort of contact in well over a decade. Now that both Levy and Sullivan have departed, the two seem prepared to trade players once again.

The two sets of fans, of course, revel in player misfortune once transfers have taken place – how West Ham supporters enjoyed Mohammed Kudus’ first season travails and then merely taking £85 million from the Spuds for the signature of Mateus Fernandes and doubling our money seemed sufficient cause for satisfaction.

Quietly banking about £20 million more than the young Portuguese would generate from any other club and heading off financial armageddon with north London money seemed a deal well done.

Spurs fans now have their moment, with the gloating evident over Manor Solomon‘s failure to launch in east London. The winger has struggled despite frequent starting slots under Nuno and must now be facing competition from young Edvin Austbø who has impressed each time he’s stepped onto the turf.

As Tottenham fan site Hotspurhq.com puts it:

“West Ham are saddled with Manor Solomon, who has scored just 2 goals with 2 assists in 14 appearances. The big problem with Solomon that Tottenham have been well aware of is that he is not a team player.

Spurs had to listen to a lot of complaining from him about his minutes or about mistreatment from the club, but the real reason why he didn’t play was because he never showed he was good enough.”

Solomon – there’s a man of the match in there lurking – but many doubt he can he return to that form once again

Identifying the problem as being specifically to do with his mindset rather than his ability, the criticism goes on:

“A big part of that is Solomon does not help his teams win. He holds the ball too much and plays like someone more focused on scoring or piling up his own stats than playing with the team.”

Early on this season, after his man of the match award, there was a feeling that we’d stolen Solomon for a very modest £4 million up – front: Depending on what a decent coaching regime can coax out of the Israeli, there may still be room for quiet satisfaction.

He has the record and the ability, but needs to find a way to return to his best form. When in a Leeds eleven, he looked a top quality prospect indeed and along with Joel Piroe scored 29 times, playing no small part in taking the club back to the Premier League.

Much like his new manager, he’s done it before and knows what is needed. The jury is out as to whether he’s still got it.

#2082. “I’m not Mo Salah” – Bradley Barcola speaks defiantly about his big-money Liverpool transfer

Bradley Barcola has said that he doesn’t feel any pressure to try and emulate Mo Salah at Liverpool and is instead focusing on creating his own legacy at Anfield.

At the end of the summer, the Reds spent an initial £106m (potentially rising to £123m, via The Athletic) to sign the French winger from Paris Saint-Germain, with the 24-year-old effectively brought in as the right-sided replacement for the Egyptian King.

It took the new signing seven matches to get off the mark for LFC, with that famine turning to feast in the form of a hat-trick against LASK in mid-October, and he’s followed that up with assists in the wins over Brentford and Brighton (Transfermarkt).

In an interview with Sky Sports, Barcola defiantly insisted that he doesn’t feel a burden to emulate Salah or repay the substantial transfer fee paid for him, with his sole focus being to make his ‘own mark’ and let his performances do the talking.

The France winger said: “First of all, I wasn’t the one who decided the transfer fee, so that’s not been my problem.

“Regarding Mo Salah, he’s a legend here, a huge one. He’s done big things here and, for that, I have an enormous respect for him, but it’s not pressure for me at all.

“I’m not Mo Salah, so I’m going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don’t feel any pressure about that.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Whoever was signed as the effective replacement for the legendary Egyptian was always going to face inevitable comparisons with our former no.11, but such were the standards set by Salah that striving to emulate him would be near-impossible.

Nobody is expecting Barcola to match the Trabzonspor man’s 257-goal tally for Liverpool over a nine-year period. As the Frenchman acknowledged, his job is simply to deliver the best that he can for the Reds.

There have been some moments to forget in his first few weeks on Merseyside, such as the missed sitter against Brentford last month, but he also conjured up a tremendous assist for Alexander Isak’s winning goal in the same match.

The 24-year-old might’ve drawn a blank against Arsenal on Sunday, but his direct running along the left flank was difficult for the Gunners to contain during the first half in particular, offering the kind of proactive threat that we love to see from wingers playing for LFC.

Salah was a unique figure at Liverpool, and Barcola doesn’t strictly have to emulate what the Egyptian has done in order to be regarded as a success at Anfield in time to come. We’ve seen glimpses of what he can offer to the Reds, and time is very much on his side to build upon that promising start.

#2080. Parker’s past threatens to haunt him over “dire football’ warning | West Ham News

Ask any West Ham fan after last weekend’s 3-1 home loss to West Bromwich Albion whether they’d settle for winning ways at all costs and most would have instantly nodded their agreement.

The second three goal loss at home within eight days had caused the boos to ring out as Nuno’s West Ham train derailed spectacularly, in what was to prove his last game and his ultimate undoing.

Right now there’s a relief flooding around the club as a former hero has returned to take over from negative Nuno. Long may it continue.

However the suggestions are that Parker may not prove to be the all-conquering hero that West Ham seek, judging from his impact at previous clubs. Yes, he knows how to get out of this division and yes, he sure can fix a porous defence – Burnley’s statistics speak for that.

But according to footballleagueworld.co.uk’s article this morning, his time at Burnley divided supporters with his grim, gritty style of play offering little in the way of entertainment:

“The football’s dire. He will bore you to death, and he will cause a fanbase to turn through little snide little comments. He will cause the West Ham fanbase to turn on it.

And that has happened at every single club consistently.”

Few will complain if Scott Parker gets West Ham promoted

Writes their Burnley fan columnist Aaron Wright, condemning Parker’s management style – not results – in the strongest possible terms.

“This is the biggest job he could get, if he can’t get them promoted slash win the league, and if he can’t then keep them in the Premier League, he needs to rethink pretty much everything. He is never getting a bigger job than this and his reputation as a player has helped him get this one. It’s the most guaranteed promotion you will ever have.

“The West Ham fans won’t enjoy it, but I think there’ll be a good respect to it if it turns out how Burnley’s did. 33 games unbeaten is something else.”

Which will have to be a price worth paying, simply to climb back out of this league after the mess of last season and save West Ham from the financial armageddon that not getting promoted would surely deliver.

To paraphrase Jacob Steiberg, Guardian journalist, on Parker’s football shortcomings not succeeding in the Premier League: worry about that next season – first you have to make it back.

#2079. Falkirk warned over Hearts injury crisis ahead of Tynecastle test

Falkirk manager John McGlynn has told his players to ignore talk of a Hearts injury crisis as they prepare for Sunday’s visit to Tynecastle.

Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken’s selection problems mounted further on Thursday when Stephen Kingsley picked up a hamstring injury in his team’s Europa League defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

Days earlier Hearts had lost Thomas Magnusson to concussion and former Falkirk midfielder Calvin Miller to a knee injury that will keep him out for two months.

Vrancken is now missing a full team of players with Harry Milne, Christian Borchgrevink, Oisin McEntee, Ageu, Craig Halkett, Blair Spittal, Tom Renaud and Oisin McEntee all out.

But McGlynn is wary of the strength in depth of his former club.

“They’ve not been beaten at home (in the league) in 18-19 months,” said McGlynn, who recently lost full-backs Leon McCann and Ryan Strain to thigh injuries.

“They’ve got a proud record there and it’s not going to be easy. Yeah, they’ve got injuries, absolutely, it’s a fact. But they can still put 11 good players on the park. They might be a little bit lighter on the bench, but they can still put a good 11 players on the pitch.

“We’re not going to get too caught up in the injuries that they have. I sympathise with the manager, he’s restricted in the players he’s got to choose from. I sympathise with the players who are getting injured.

“But we’ve got to focus on our job and not get too caught up in that.

“You end up coming a cropper if you’re thinking that they’ve got all these players injured, and it’s just a matter of turning up.

“We know that’s not going to be the case and that’s the message that I’m giving to our players.”

Vrancken told Hearts TV: “The situation we’re in, we have to just stick together and fight again on Sunday.

“It’s an important run of games like we already know, and make sure that we are as fit as possible to go for the game.

“It is good that it’s a Tynecastle, so we have a full stadium behind us and that has to give the energy to make it this last game before the break a good one.”

‘But we really didn’t dominate the game. We had more possession, but Newcastle was fine with that. In terms of chances, it was very equal.’

‘I gave Leno a bit of stick earlier in the season, but he has certainly redeemed himself by much improved performances recently, and he will deservedly win MOTM. The save against Lewis Hall at the end make me jump out of my seat. I felt like it was all huff and puff from us today without much end product. A step down from recent performances where we should have scored 5 in each if we could finish at all. Great to see Muniz reinvigorated, and hopefully he can help with that problem going forward. The referee had a good game.’

‘Fair result in the end as really not much in it between both sides. Thought Bassey and Leno were our best players, but a big shoutout to Berge in the first half as he was immense. Iwobi I thought was also very good first half. We started the second half slow and that gave Newcastle a bit more belief; Palacios was great when he came on IMO, as was Muniz.’

‘Two fairly evenly matched teams settled for some dull stuff in the first half and Newcastle came out after the break far perkier than our lads. Draw is a reasonable result under circumstances.

Not sure I learned much new about our team or individuals. Thought I’d sleep on it before posting, perhaps some inspiration would arrive overnight. It hasn’t. Palacios is obviously going to be a fine player, but it’s equally obvious that we are something of a learning experience for him and that pass was a mistake of callow youth.

As an England supporter, Lewis Hall’s performance was a small comfort. To these eyes, the best player on the pitch.’ 🎙️ THE MAG PODCAST Ep 13: Newcastle United beat Palace, Schar and Burn Deliver, and Eddie Howe to Man Utd? Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! #2075. Veltman’s West Ham Admission Highlights Parker’s First Big Problem

West Ham defender Joël Veltman has admitted that the Hammers’ habit of starting matches poorly must change, with Scott Parker facing an immediate challenge against Blackburn Rovers this afternoon.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Veltman acknowledged that Wednesday’s disastrous first half against Cardiff City was hardly an isolated incident. West Ham recovered from three goals down to draw 3-3, but the Dutchman knows they cannot keep relying on second-half comebacks.

“It wasn’t the first time we haven’t started so well,” admitted Veltman, who wants West Ham to begin against Blackburn with the same intensity they showed after the interval in Wales.

Personally, I think West Ham’s slow starts and early capitulations are definitely a mentality problem. Nothing demonstrated that more clearly than the transformation at half-time against Cardiff, when a team that had looked completely traumatised and shell-shocked suddenly emerged looking like an entirely different side.

Of course, some of that improvement was tactical, but I’m not entirely convinced how many tactics you can impart in 15 minutes. What Parker, Mark Noble and Jarrod Bowen clearly managed to do was give the players a lift, and the difference in their attitude was extraordinary.

I’ve thought from day one that this was probably the easiest improvement any new manager could make with the current group of players. If West Ham approach matches with a positive attitude and a genuine desire to win rather than playing fearfully, I suspect much of the problem could be addressed with a decent team talk.

That doesn’t mean tactics and team selection are irrelevant, but the players have already demonstrated they possess considerably more ability than their recent performances suggest. Parker’s first job is surely to convince them of that.

Veltman himself was absolutely brilliant during the second half against Cardiff, and I think he could become an important player under Parker. His composure and positioning at right-back could allow Jarrod Bowen the freedom to drift into central areas, where the West Ham captain caused absolute havoc on Wednesday evening.

Bowen was instrumental in the comeback, and having a dependable defender behind him could make that attacking freedom much easier to accommodate. It’s another reason why I’d like to see Veltman retain his place against Blackburn.

The defender certainly recognises the opportunity ahead, telling the club: “We want to go into another away game on Saturday and start where we finished.”

That really is the challenge for Parker. West Ham don’t need to discover some previously hidden ability between now and kick-off; they need to reproduce the confidence, aggression and positive mentality they finally showed during those remarkable 45 minutes against Cardiff.

#2074. An open letter to Newcastle United fans

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!
