#2029. Rangers 'doing everything' to stop Ryan Naderi joining new club - Transfer Expert

Rangers are bracing to receive interest in Ryan Naderi after his strong start to the season, sources have told Football Insider.

The 23-year-old has established himself as a crucial part of Derek McInnes' plans for the season, particularly in the absence of some of the Ibrox club's other attacking options.

He has made 17 appearances across all competitions so far, scored nine goals and provided five assists, with a number of high-profile suitors alerted to his form.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Rangers are prepared to do everything in their power to keep Naderi at the club long term.

The Czechia international will be key to any success McInnes' side enjoy this season, having already fired them to the League Cup final with a goal contribution in every round.

Regardless of the interest from clubs across European football, Naderi is likely to remain at Rangers beyond the January transfer window, as offers will not be entertained.

Former Everton CEO Keith Wyness told Football Insider that Rangers are likely to capitalise on Naderi's popularity with the supporters as part of their commercial efforts.

The forward has quickly become a fans' favourite at Ibrox alongside his impressive performances, which have wowed everybody watching including his suitors.

However, regardless of the interest from elsewhere, Rangers have big plans for Naderi and are hopeful of keeping him at Ibrox beyond the January transfer window.

"Rangers will be doing everything in their power to keep their best players at the club," Brown told Football Insider.

"That includes somebody like Naderi, who has been outstanding for them so far this season, and his recent performances have shown how important he can be.

"Obviously, when a player is performing at such a high level for Rangers, he's going to attract interest from some other top clubs.

"Clubs in the Premier League, for example, will have scouts watching Rangers every week and I don't doubt they will have been impressed by what they've seen from Naderi.

"But from a Rangers point of view, they want him to keep being an important player for them, and they need to keep their best players if they want to win silverware.

"So I would be very surprised if they were prepared to let Naderi leave mid-way through the season, regardless of whether anybody else is keen."

Transfer rumours are swirling around Rangers at the moment, with speculation about incoming and outgoing deals picking up ahead of the January window.

Naderi is unlikely to be allowed to leave, but others could be, whether that is in the mid-season window or next summer, as McInnes looks to find a balance in his squad.

Wyness told Football Insider on 8 November that Rangers could look to cash in on Youssef Chermiti when he returns from injury near the end of this season.

Chermiti, 22, is currently expected to be out until the latter stages of the season with his ACL injury, which he suffered days after Rangers rejected a £22million bid in the summer.

That would then free up funds to agree a permanent deal for Badredine Bouanani, who has impressed since making his way into the first-team squad under McInnes.

#2028. 'When you look at the video...' - Ex-refs chief shares Cole Palmer penalty verdict after re-analysing Chelsea vs Sunderland footage

Cole Palmer and Chelsea should have been awarded a penalty in the first half of Sunday's 1-0 defeat to Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

That is according to former head of PGMOL and FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The incident came mid-way through the first half just minutes before Levi Colwill was adjudged to have brought down Brian Brobbey in the penalty area.

Enzo Le Fee converted the spot kick and put Sunderland ahead, with Chelsea unable to fight their way back into the game.

Xabi Alonso felt that his team should have had an earlier penalty, however, with Palmer felled by Luke O'Nien as he looked to drive into the box.

Jarred Gillett initially ignored the incident, with VAR Nick Hopton eventually deeming that the contact came outside the penalty box.

Thoughts? No foul, no penalty for that challenge on Cole Palmer?! Make it make sense! 🙄 #Chelsea #SUNCHE pic.twitter.com/UgIg3aH0WK

Alonso will feel that Chelsea had the worst of it by VAR in Saturday's game, and rightly so.

Sunderland's penalty was an extremely harsh decision, with Brobbey clearly having hold of Levi Colwill's shirt before he went down.

And Palmer was clearly fouled, with Gillett inexplicably failing to even award a free-kick.

VAR did determine that O'Nien had gone through the back and fouled Palmer, but was happy to confirm that contact took place outside of the box.

Replays have called that decision into question, however, with the challenge seemingly arriving when the Chelsea man is on the line of the penalty box.

"When you look at the video, it appears that Cole Palmer has been fouled outside of the penalty area," Hackett told Football Insider.

"However, the still image shows that Palmer's foot is on the line. The line forms part of the penalty area, and therefore Chelsea are rather unfortunate not to be awarded a penalty kick."

While both controversial decisions on Sunday would have affected the game, there is little doubt that Chelsea did not deserve three points.

The Blues were bettered in every area, and were ultimately fortunate not to concede more.

"I haven’t seen Cole’s actions, but there could be a chance that it could be given," said Alonso after the game.

"We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win," he added, keen not to find excuses.

Nottingham Forest have been struggling this season, but the return of Ryan Yates to the starting XI on Saturday gave them an added boost.

His energy and willingness to get stuck into challenges brought a different dimension to Forest's midfield.

And it was perhaps a reminder that Glasner has got his treatment of the skipper all wrong this season.

Forest have lacked the aggression and defensive discipline needed to compete consistently this season.

Glasner's side often come up against teams that want to dominate the ball, and those tenacious midfielders are needed.

Additionally, only Xaver Schlager's 14 defensive contributions were more than the Englishman's 11, and he did not play the full game after coming off in the 79th minute.

The presence and mere leadership of the 28-year-old was exactly what had been missing from Glasner's Nottingham Forest, and Yates should now go from fringe star to regular starter.

And that could be a game- and season-changing decision from the Austrian manager.

Yates may not be the most technically gifted midfielder, or the nicest player to watch on the eye.

Too often this season, Forest have looked short of fight, and when it comes to the Englishman, that is something you know you will never have a lack of.

Having a player who is willing to do the ugly work and set the standard for those around him is invaluable.

Yates has demonstrated that he can provide exactly that, and Glasner must recognise it.

The midfielder must be a regular feature following the upcoming international break.

#2024. Martin O'Neill 'leapt out of his seat in utter disbelief' after what he saw in Celtic win vs Kilmarnock

Correspondent AUTHORITY NCTJ-qualified football journalist with experience at VAVEL, Hayters TV, SPORTbible, and Centredevils. Martin O'Neill was incensed when Kasper Hogh's opener for Celtic against Kilmarnock on Sunday was disallowed.

The Hoops ultimately won 1-0, with the breakthrough provided midway through the first half by Liam Scales.

The pressure was on at Parkhead, with the champions responding to failure to win any of their previous two Scottish Premiership clashes.

But had Celtic not found the breakthrough, a serious inquest into Hogh's disallowed goal would have undoubtedly followed.

The 25-year-old's strike had initially been allowed, before referee John Beaton was sent to the monitor for another look.

He did not take a long time to come to a decision, disallowing the goal and awarding a free-kick for a challenge by Mika Baur earlier in the move.

15’ - 🖥️ VAR Check: Goal ruled out due to a foul in the build up.🟩0️⃣-0️⃣🟨#CELKIL | #CelticFC🍀 https://t.co/KiDyM93QWh

Celtic ultimately should have extended their lead in the second half, but the game remained close.

Benjamin Nygren saw his penalty saved, while others missed other great chances to put the game to bed.

And it almost came back to bite them, with Ieuan Owen going extremely close to finding the net in the final minutes.

It could well have been a very different game if Hogh's goal had been allowed to stand, however.

The summer signing looked to have finally broken his goal duck, which has plagued him since his hat-trick against Kilmarnock at the start of August.

It was a good finish, too, but it would be chalked off just minutes later when Beaton was advised to go to the screen.

Mika Baur was adjudged to have fouled Greg Kiltie in the build-up, seemingly going through the man to get to the ball.

The decision was a soft one, and O'Neill was far from impressed. "Martin O’Neill leapt out of his seat in utter disbelief, there," Amy Canavan told BBC Sport Scotland.

"On first viewing, Mika Baur’s nudge looked minimal, but John Beaton didn’t spend much time at the monitor."

Ultimately, O'Neill will have been pleased to see his way come away with the three points, ending a difficult run of form.

Celtic have opened a four-point gap at the top of the table for the time being, with Rangers holding a game in hand.

"After Thursday night's exertions, I thought we were not at our very, very best today," O'Neill told Celtic TV.

"Having said that, we created a number of good chances in the game. Sam Johnstone makes a big, big save - a double save for us in the first 90 seconds - and we're just really delighted to have won.

"Big, big effort Thursday night, coming back on Sunday again, and we got the breakthrough and we won."

Neither side could find a winner in the second half but United have now extended their unbeaten run to seven games to remain sixth in the table while Motherwell stay ninth.

The Steelmen took the lead in the ninth minute. Tawanda Maswanhise tumbled in the home box under a challenge from Dylan Tait but the linesman’s flag went up for offside.

However, referee Ryan Lee was called over to the pitchside monitor by the VAR Andrew Dallas and decided to award a penalty. Fadinger stepped up and sent United goalkeeper Jack Walton the wrong way.

Shortly after, United were claiming for a penalty of their own when Zac Sapsford went down in a challenge with Emmanuel Longelo but the whistler flashed a yellow card at the Terrors striker for diving.

Maswanhise then created an opening of his own, embarking on a barnstorming run but his shot flew straight to Walton, who easily gathered.

Motherwell’s Ibrahim Said was next to try his luck from 22 yards but again his effort was straight at Walton and then Sapsford hit a snap-shot that was well saved by the visitors’ goalie Alexander Paulsen.

Walton was called into action again in the 28th minute when Tom Sparrow found Longelo inside the United box with the defender hitting a shot into the ground that the keeper had to acrobatically tip over, before Daniel Bennie went close at the other end with a header.

Paulsen then made two smart saves in quick succession from shots by Lyall Cameron and then Tait.

However, the keeper could not prevent United equalising in the 41st minute when the ball found its way to Randall inside the Motherwell box and with his back to the goal, the New Zealander produced a cheeky backheel that flew past Paulsen.

Randall had another chance at the start of the second half but this time his composure deserted him and he blasted well over the bar.

Longelo then found himself in a promising position but his curling shot was deflected for a corner.

The hosts hit back with Bennie cutting in from the left before striking a fierce shot that was well blocked by Motherwell defender Martin Moorman.

There was a big scare for the hosts in the 62nd minute when Bert Esselink was robbed of possession by Seb Palmer-Houlden but the striker’s shot flew just over.

It was United’s turn to threaten next with Michael Forbes producing a powerful header that was cleared off the line by Moorman.

The hosts had a great chance to snatch a winner in the 87th minute but Josh Rawlins completely fluffed his lines just two yards with Randall then coming close with a shot.

Chris Kavanagh had a mixed evening at Old Trafford as Aston Villa drew 4-4 with Man United.

When Matheus Cunha was fouled in the 14th minute, the referee got it absolutely spot on by awarding a penalty.

And then he was correct not to rule out Man United's equalising goal at 2-2, when Mbuemo was in fact onside while blocking Zion Suzuki's view.

The foul by Diogo Dalot on Alysson in the second half was also spot-on, with the away side getting a penalty of their own.

However, not all of his decisions were correct at Old Trafford, with Kavanagh coming away with a mixed record.

With many contentious decisions still to discuss throughout the 90 minutes, Football Insider takes a look at three errors the Englishman made while officiating the clash.

In the eighth minute of the match, Kavanagh had his positioning all wrong, leading to Man United missing out on an open player to pass to.

The referee found himself right at the centre of a United attack, and as he took steps back to get out of the way, he managed to step on Fernandes.

The Portuguese midfielder's lane to receive the ball was then blocked by the official, al and he hopped in pain, as Villa would then regain the ball.

Not a great start for the referee, who had a number of important decisions set to come up.

Just before half-time, Fernandes had gone in high on Villa winger Alysson, with the Brazilian ending up on the floor inside the box.

It was quite reckless from the Portuguese midfielder, and on replay, it showed he did not get the ball.

VAR did check over the incident, but no penalty was awarded to the away side.

Fernandes is lucky to have escaped giving a penalty away on that occasion, although many could argue there was limited contact.

In the 72nd minute, United defender Leny Yoro went in quite strongly on Johan Manzambi, leaving the Swiss international in pen and requiring treatment.

Replays showed that the Villa man was struck first before the ball, but Kavanagh instead gave a throw-in.

The tackle was one that should have been awarded a booking and a free-kick to the away side.

#2019. Ex-refs chief: VAR should have 'intervened' over Sunderland penalty in win vs Chelsea

The penalty that ultimately saw Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 on Sunday should have been overturned.

That is according to former head of PGMOL and FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

Enzo Le Fee made no mistake from the penalty, which was awarded by Jarred Gillett for Levi Colwill's foul on Brian Brobbey.

Xabi Alonso was incensed, as were his players, who felt that the defender had been dragged down by the Sunderland striker.

The Black Cats continued to threaten and were ultimately unlucky not to add to their advantage, with Chelsea struggling to make an impact.

The defeat leaves the Blues behind Liverpool and already 11 points adrift of Premier League leaders, Arsenal.

WE HAVE BEEN SCAMMED. #CFCpic.twitter.com/bKbfWJ8QWT

Upon seeing the replays, many would have almost assumed that VAR would overturn the decision.

While Colwill was behind Brobbey and certainly had a hold of his shirt, there was also sustained holding by the Sunderland striker.

The Dutchman quite clearly had hold of the England international's sleeve, before ultimately clipping his own legs on his way down.

But Gillett awarded the penalty after a brief pause and VAR Nick Hopton ultimately confirmed the decision, much to the anger of Chelsea.

"In my opinion, the Sunderland penalty kick awarded by referee Jarred Gillett should've seen the intervention of VAR," Hackett told Football Insider.

"Review of the video shows that the Sunderland player is in fact the offender, holding his opponent by the shirt and dragging him to the ground behind him. Not a penalty kick for me."

Interestingly, Sunderland also benefitted from a similar incident earlier in the season at the Stadium of Light.

The visit of Arsenal had been closely-contested, before John Brooks pointed to the spot for a penalty for the home side for a seemingly obvious foul.

Replays clearly showed that Dan Ballard had grabbed hold of Ezri Konsa's shirt and pulled him to the ground in a judo roll, but the penalty stood.

David Raya produced the save that day and Arsenal would ultimately win - Chelsea were not so lucky on Sunday.

#2018. First meeting against a team 20 unbeaten: All the key stats ahead of Milan vs. Ferencvaros

The first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros will take place at San Siro this evening in the Europa League.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

So, tonight’s contest is an unprecedented one, and it pits two teams together that have made very different starts to their Europa League campaigns.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match.

➤ Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencváros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026-27.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing.

➤ The Diavolo suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11.

➤ Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures.

➤ Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967-68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level.

➤ Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

#2017. St Johnstone 2-1 Dundee: Hosts edge derby thriller with deflected winner

A deflected Kai Fotheringham strike on 72 minutes dealt Dundee their first defeat at St Johnstone for five years.

Josh Campbell scored the second headed goal of his loan from Hibernian to earn Saints a fifth-minute lead.

Substitute striker Joe Westley seized on a defensive howler to level just after halftime.

Fotheringham capped an excellent return from a two-match suspension to secure a 2-1 victory with his first goal since William Hill Premiership opening weekend.

Simo Valakari’s side won their fourth league game since returning to the top-flight and moved level on 17 points with their Tayside rivals.

Owen Bevan returned from injury to replace Joe Wright in Steven Pressley’s only change.

Reece McAlear’s illness forced Valakari into one of four switches that also included top-scorer Josh Fowler dropping to the bench.

Danny Schmidt recovered from an ankle knock to lead the line as Saints set the tone with a high-tempo and profitable opening spell.

Bosnian full-back Enes Alic swung over a terrific delivery to the near post. No Dundee defender was wise to the ghosting run of Campbell who arrived on cue to head emphatically past Owen Goodman.

Saints defender Bozo Mikulic was forced off with a facial knock on 14 minutes. Dan Finlayson replaced the Croatian and that defensive switch was not put under great strain in the first 45.

Dundee threatened only in the 24th minute when captain Ethan Hamilton’s surprise shot on the turn was diverted for a corner by Ross Sinclair.

Saints could easily have doubled their advantage three minutes before half-time. Alic conjured a fierce hit from 25 yards, parried out by Goodman. The rebound fell for Taylor Steven who snatched at the ball and shot well wide.

That missed opportunity came back to haunt the Saints quickly after the interval.

Finlayson ushered a header back towards Sinclair but, as the keeper came to gather, a collision with Cheick Diabate caused a spillage.

Westley, one of three halftime introductions, accepted the gift and found the empty net with ease. Saints, as they have done all season, responded well to a setback. Campbell went close at the near post and a full-stretch Goodman’s fingertips brushed a 30-yard dig from Cotterill just wide.

They wrested back the lead with a terrific transition move. Hamilton gave the ball away and Saints swiftly broke. After great work from Liam Smith down the right, Campbell’s blocked effort spun up for Fotheringham.

His shot took a heavy deflection to leave Goodman rooted to the spot as the ball sailed in.

Dundee had the ball in the net through Ryan Finnigan on 79 minutes. However, referee David Dickinson penalised Owen Bevan for a push in the penalty box melee.

And an offside flag denied Macaulay Tait a tap-in third for Saints. Dundee spurned one fine chance at an equaliser in stoppage time.

Westley scuffed his attempt from six yards, and Sinclair was relieved to gather.

Aston Villa and Manchester United were held to a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.

This fixture was filled with action, with four goals in the first half, including a rapid-fire start from the away side, followed by four more in the second.

Villa had gone 2-0 up within just four minutes, but Man United battled their way back into the game.

The away side, though, would respond better when the second half kicked off, restoring their two-goal lead but ultimately the home side brought it level in the end.

However, while the goals and penalty incidents will get the headlines, there were some moments that likely went amiss for supporters.

As Football Insider looks at the things you may have missed amid all the chaotic action at Old Trafford.

Protests against the current structure of Manchester United's board continued against Aston Villa.

In the Stretford End, a sign stating: "We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners" could be seen hung up.

Green and yellow balloons, detailing the historic colours of the club, were plentiful in the stand as well before the game had even kicked off.

It was far from what Michael Carrick wanted from his players when Man United went 2-0 down after just four minutes.

The home crowd were also far from amused, and chants telling the players they were "not fit to wear the shirt" went around the ground.

However, when the half-time whistle went, the cheers were incredibly loud, with the players on the pitch turning the toxicity around.

It didn't take long for Youri Tielemans to hear how Aston Villa fans are feeling months on from his departure.

In the ninth minute, there were audible boos from the away end towards the Belgian midfielder.

Tielemans would go on to score the equalising goal at 2-2, but it seems he was not willing to hit back at his former club as he refused to celebrate.

While Villa started well against Manchester United, manager Unai Emery was left fuming with a couple of his players.

In the first half, the Villans were losing the ball in avoidable situations.

As per reporter Jacob Tanswell, Emery was left frustrated with his players' decision-making early in the first half, with Johan Manzambi and Ian Maatsen in particular.

Suzuki saves Cunha’s curling effort. #AVFC surely have to drop Alysson deeper as Harwood-Bellis is having to defend in wide areas and United are getting joy.Emery unhappy with Maatsen & Manzambi just now. Wanted both to turn back and keep the ball. His deeper players are…

Instead of looking to keep possession, the pair opted to try to bring the ball forward, ultimately giving it away.

During the broadcast of the match, TV cameras panned to talk about Robin van Persie and his volley that won United their 20th league title against Aston Villa in 2013.

However, another Old Trafford familiar face was beside him, but did not even get a mention.

That was former striker Javier Hernandez, who had played 157 times for the Red Devils over his career.

#2014. GdS: A combined salary less than Ramos’ – the story behind the Ferencvaros ‘miracle’

AC Milan’s opponents Ferencvaros are one of a few teams to have a perfect record in the Europa League, and their story is a fascinating one.

Ferencváros arrive at San Siro having won all three of their league phase games thus far. In addition to that, they are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and they will go top of their domestic league if they win their game in hand. La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) share some insight on the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gonçalo Ramos’s gross salary €12.8m (€7m net including bonuses) is equivalent to the entire wage bill of Ferencváros. The combined salaries of the Hungarian club’s players total €11m.

Their highest earner is Naby Keïta, who accepted a contract worth just over €1.2m gross per season, seeking a career resurgence at the club with the largest payroll in the Hungarian league.

The Serbian midfielder Birmančević – formerly of Sparta Prague and Getafe, who arrived last summer – earns a slightly lower salary. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Zachariassen earns around €700k and has scored three goals so far, as has Alphadjo Cissé.

In terms of wages, therefore, there is simply no comparison between the Rossoneri and Ferencváros. Yet, the Hungarians have won every match, while Milan have only three points. All the more reason not to take them lightly.

Gabor Kubatov has been on the board of Ferencváros since 2010, becoming president a year later. Under his leadership, the club has won eight Hungarian league titles. His personal history is quite unique: as a young man, he was a regular in ‘Sector 2’ – the section occupied by the ultras.

He later changed paths, and in 2006, he became a member of parliament, representing Fidesz, the party of Viktor Orbán. Despite his own background in the stands, his relationship with the Ferencváros ultras has not always been smooth.

In 2014, in an effort to combat violence and incidents of racism, Kubatov introduced a biometric identification system for stadium entry. A segment of the most ardent supporters responded by boycotting home matches, a protest that lasted for over three years.

An agreement was finally reached and the fans returned to the stands. With their support, Ferencváros went on to win seven consecutive league titles.

On 10 December 2017, a young Adam Nagy faced Milan while playing for Bologna. It didn’t go well: a 2-1 victory for the Rossoneri. Today, Nagy returns as a far more mature leader of his ‘miracle’ Ferencváros side.

Indeed, a significant portion of the Hungarian midfielder’s career has unfolded in Italy. He spent three years with the Rossoblù from 2016 to 2019 – following his initial breakthrough at Ferencváros – before returning to Italy in 2021 to join Pisa, having previously left to try his hand at Bristol City in England.

His most recent stint was with Spezia, which he departed this summer to return to his homeland. Yesterday, in a press conference, Rúben Amorim spoke very highly of him: “He is very skilled in the initial phase of build-up play.”

His ability to circulate the ball deep in his own half is his greatest strength. Conversely, he rarely ventures into the final third. The proof? Throughout all his years in Italy, he scored only one goal: against Verona in Serie A.

From the European champions Liverpool to Ferencvaros. Naby Keita – who will start on the bench tonight, hasn’t had the career he hoped for. Liverpool paid €65m to sign him from RB Leipzig in 2018, he won six more trophies in addition to the Champions League with Klopp’s English side.

In 2023, the Guinean midfielder moved to Werder Bremen, where he was left out of the squad after refusing to travel for the trip to Leverkusen because he wouldn’t have been a starter. Since January 2025, he has been at Ferencváros, who acquired him a year later.

Wearing a Liverpool shirt, Keïta has already beaten Milan at San Siro on 7 December 2021, a defeat that contributed to the Diavolo being eliminated in the group stage.

A less pleasant memory for Keïta involves his encounter with Luka Modrić when he came on in the final minutes of the 2022 Champions League final, which Liverpool lost to Real Madrid.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider’s Transfer Insider podcast, 26-year-old Yeboah is a target for the Eagles but they face competition from other top-flight sides.

Everton are known to be keen on his services, while Ipswich are also eyeing the Italian striker to aid their Premier League survival bid.

Yeboah has 18 goals and four assists in 32 MLS appearances for Minnesota so far this season.

Palace are the league's third-lowest scorers up to now, and Jean-Phillippe Mateta and Jorgen Strand Larsen have just one goal between them in the top flight since August, so a new addition may well be needed in January.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "My understanding is that the three Premier League clubs that are probably most interested in Kelvin Yeboah right now are Everton, Crystal Palace and Ipswich. They're the ones that are keeping tabs on the Minnesota United striker.

"There is an opportunity for a number of Premier League clubs to strike because he’s going into the final 13 months of his contract, expiring in December 2027, and he has done very well for Minnesota. I’m sure there’ll be interest from those clubs I mentioned, probably in January."

Yeboah clearly has plans to emulate his uncle, but may instead be lining up for an opponent at Elland Road in the near future.

The Minnesota striker admitted in a February 2026 interview with Gianluca DiMarzio that he harbours ambitions of featuring in the English top flight at some point soon.

He said: "I dream of the Premier League...it is my biggest objective. I believe that type of football is also the most suitable for me. I hope one day I can afford myself a ticket to play in that league. Physically, [MLS] is similar to the Premier League, whereas in Serie A they concentrate mainly on tactics."

#2012. The tactical 'freedom' Celtic give Callum Osmand and his unlikely Camilo Duran bond

With Celtic a goal behind against Besiktas in the 60th minute, on came Callum Osmand. His impact was almost instantaneous, equalising with his first touch and, soon after, setting up fellow substitute Camilo Duran with a refined reverse pass.

Martin O'Neill said it was all part of the masterplan. The Celtic manager rotated his XI heavily before calling on the cavalry come the hour.

Osmand's influence on the 3-2 victory was profound. He enthused the home support with fresh attacking impetus, haring at Besiktas' defence and providing that crucial end product.

Although Osmand averages a goal or assist every 90 minutes this season, he concedes he must improve.

"I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally, and there's stuff I need to tidy up on, decision-making and all this stuff," Osmand said. "But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

"So on a personal note, that's what I want to do, just keep learning and keep understanding my role, like the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

"And I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning, but I feel like when you get thrown in at the deep end, it's the best way to learn, and the worst games are what you learn off more than the good games.

"It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on."

Osmand joined Celtic from Fulham last summer as a central striker, yet since the defeat to Benfica last month, he's been moulded into a left winger.

Learning a new position isn't easy, though Osmand likes the freedom that comes with playing out wide.

"It is new for me, but I'm really enjoying it," he said. "It's a really fun position and it's very, very attacking.

"I have a lot of freedom and the staff give me that freedom and tell me to go and try and make something happen. So it's a great feeling when you know you can just go and sort of impose your game."

Osmand did exactly that on Thursday evening. O'Neill told him to 'just go' before coming on, instructing the 20-year-old to bring the energy that gets supporters on their feet.

"I think that's the best feeling in football, when you can get everyone behind you and it feels amazing, so that's what I sort of strive for, that feeling," Osmand said.

His presence helped flip the game on its head, offering Celtic fresh hope of Europa League progression after defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica, and Celta Vigo.

O'Neill's side can look ahead to their trip to Torreense later this month knowing it means something.

"For us, it felt like a must win, that was our sort of mindset going into that. This was sort of it," Osmand said of the Besiktas game. "Like we knew we could still qualify, but we knew we had to get something out of Thursday night, and I think the boys done amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this.

"We have some tougher away ties, but hopefully we can use that and just use this, and that gives us confidence to play more free, and take more risks.

"Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play, but as you can see, when we're confident, it just goes forward every time, and it's a good feeling, so hopefully we can build on that."

For Celtic, wins like Thursday's have proven rare this season. There was a real sense of togetherness at the full-time whistle.

O'Neill raised his right fist to the heavens in celebration before gracing the turf and embracing his players.

Osmand knows Celtic haven't been at their best of late. Last weekend's defeat at Falkirk sparked some all too familiar emotions.

Thursday sent Celtic to the other end of the spectrum. Now they must stay there.

"I think we know that we're a good side," Osmand said. "We all back each other, and I think when we're all together, and the fans are with us, and you feel it, you just want to get everyone sort of on one page, and then we feel like an amazing team.

"It's sometimes tough to get to that point, because we're lacking confidence, or we're not playing as well, but I think Thursday night really showed everyone was together, and the final whistle gave us that. It should give us that confidence to go on."

Osmand dovetailed superbly with Duran after coming on against Besiktas, setting up the Colombian striker's first goal of the triumph.

That relationship extends beyond the pitch, even if a language barrier remains.

On Duran, Osmand said: "He's unbelievable, a really top player. You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

"I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy.

"His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot. I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

"And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy."

You wouldn't bet against Duran and Osmand once again coming to the fore when Celtic host Kilmarnock in the William Hill Premiership on Sunday afternoon.

The champions defeated Neil McCann's side 5-1 at Rugby Park back in August. A similar result would go a long way to building on the positive feeling triggered by Thursday's victory.

"I think sometimes when you don't give a team that's obviously not doing as well respect, then you can get caught, and sometimes you don't want to get too overconfident going into these games, because then you'll get caught out," Osmand added.

"I think it's just giving every team you play respect, and knowing that most teams can hurt us, and we have to just go in with the same mentality as Thursday night, and hopefully get a good result.

"I think it's really important for the league. Obviously, we're still at the top of the league, but obviously the gap can change at any time, so it's just about winning every game possible in the league, and just building on everything."

The 74-year-old is under fire as a result of a string of inconsistent displays at Parkhead, with serious questions asked over his position following last week's defeat against Falkirk.

Since then, a 3-2 win against Besiktas secured the Hoops their first Europa League points of the season, and the board are hoping that result will kickstart a ressurgence.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Celtic remain firmly behind O'Neill and hope he will see out the remainder of his contract.

Regardless of how their results go this season, the manager is expected to leave next summer, having penned a one-year deal to stay on following his initial interim spell.

That will then allow Celtic to take their time and bring in the ideal replacement, rather than being forced into a decision by pulling the trigger mid-way through the season.

McKenna would be available to step straight into the role, having left his position at Ipwich Town following their promotion in the summer, and is high on Celtic's list.

#2010. GdS: Milan’s €500m Adidas deal causes reaction from rivals Inter – the situation

Inter are looking enviously at their city rivals AC Milan once again after Saturday’s derby, with the news of the record Adidas deal emerging.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport on Wednesday, under the new agreement Adidas will pay Milan €50m per year for ten seasons starting from 2028-29. This is when the collaboration with PUMA ends, who currently pay €24.5m per year, as per the last accounts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The paper (via Calciomercato.com) go on to state that it is likely that the €50m yearly figure includes sporting bonuses, such as participation in the Champions League, the value of material supplies (value in kind) and a portion to be invested in promotional activities (marketing fund).

Contracts with kit makers are not limited to recognising the value of just the home, away, third and other shirts, but can extend to the sale of related products. Then, guaranteed minimums and royalties come into play that are triggered above a certain turnover threshold.

For example, in addition to the €24.5m from PUMA, €55.8m in revenues came from store, e-commerce and merchandising/licensing activities, in particular those relating to the contract with the same German company and those from licensing with Fanatics and MatchWornShirt.

As for Inter, the renewal with Nike – effective from 2023 – resulted in a 70% increase over the previous contract, but the €28m per year is not in line with the club’s current commercial value. In addition to the Milan-Adidas deal, Juventus currently get €46m per year from Adidas (€41m from 2027-28).

Inter have maintained their merchandising revenues internally, over €35m in 2025-26 thanks to the new business model introduced with Fanatics, but Nike’s €28m is too little according to the Nerazzurri’s commercial management.

The contract expires in 2031, and La Gazzetta report that they will seek to renegotiate the deal to avoid accumulating delays over the next five years. Considering that Juventus and Milan have committed to the next decade, Inter have leverage as the only one of the ‘big three’ up for grabs.

That is according to former Aberdeen chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the Ibrox chief will be “tempted” to trigger the club’s £15million purchase option for the winger.

Bouanani has broken into the starting XI in recent weeks and is catching the eye with his direct style and quick feet.

Wyness believes that Cavenagh’s impending deal to sell his ParetoHealth company could potentially be used to help fund the permanent acquisition of Bouanani.

The 21-year-old is on loan from Stuttgart at the moment and is quickly becoming a firm favourite among the Rangers fans.

The Algerian has already chipped in with a goal and an assist so far in Scottish Premiership action, and could be a crucial part of Derek McInnes’ plans moving forward.

Aberdeen’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Pittodrie between 2000 and 2004 and now runs a consultancy business advising elite clubs – believes that Cavenagh could personally fund a move for Bouanani if ParetoHealth are sold.

Recent reports in America have suggested that the company is worth an eye-watering £4.5billion, which could see Cavenagh net a huge chunk of cash in the coming months.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained how he may be tempted to invest part of that into Rangers’ transfer budget.

“The one other story that we talked about recently was Andrew Cavenagh, the chairman, selling his ParetoHealth and he's now cashed up personally,” he said.

#2008. Sam Johnstone's honest Celtic results admission as dressing room mood revealed

Goalkeeper Sam Johnstone admits Celtic have fallen below expectations this season, with recent form impacting the team's spirit.

Thursday's 3-2 victory over Besiktas, Johnstone says, showed their character, with the long-term target now to 'put things right'.

The stopper, signed on loan from Wolverhampton Wanderers during the summer transfer window, has started Celtic's last five matches, displacing Viljami Sinisalo between the sticks.

"The expectation, rightly so, for this place is to win games," Johnstone said. "Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation, and the lads know that. We try to win every game and put things right."

Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone walks off the pitch at half-time. (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

Celtic had won just three of their previous ten matches before Besiktas.

Beating the Turks, then, was crucial in repairing the mood, both internally and externally.

"I think the results affect it," Johnstone said of the spirit within the camp. "This club's not used to losing, and we’ve probably lost too many games for this club.

"We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game. The lads go out to win every game, so the camp is good.

"It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people, and honest with each other. You could see on Thursday night that the lads put a good fight in and got the result."

Johnstone's recent run of starts is his most consistent since joining Celtic at the start of September.

The 33-year-old was thrust in shortly after signing, playing against St Johnstone in the William Hill Premiership and Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup.

He failed to impress in the 3-0 defeat at Ibrox but now looks far more assured.

"To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm," Johnstone explained. "It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.

"Listen, to get the games and to keep going and get the win on Thursday night was a good feeling.

"It's brilliant to play for this club. The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training.

"When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here."

After their first Europa League win of the season, Celtic's focus shifts back to the domestic scene, where Kilmarnock lie in wait on Sunday afternoon.

Returning to winning ways in the Premiership after last weekend's defeat to Falkirk is key.

Man United's hierarchy are reluctant to sack Michael Carrick because of their recent track record of hiring and firing managers, sources have told Football Insider.

#2005. Liverpool already have Alisson replacement in place as exit nears

Giorgi Mamardashvili is well-placed to step into the starting XI when Alisson leaves Liverpool, sources have told Football Insider.

The 26-year-old has been forced to bide his time since making the move to Anfield from Valencia in 2025, with the Brazil international still regarded as the first-choice goalkeeper.

However, after multiple error-prone performances so far this season, contingency plans are being put in place for Alisson to leave Liverpool when his contract expires.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Mamardashvili is ready to push for a place in the starting XI under Andoni Iraola.

The Georgia international has made just two appearances so far this season, both of which came in the Carabao Cup, but has frequently filled in when Alisson has been unavailable.

Having come to the club with ambitions of landing a starting role, there is now a growing belief that, should Alisson leave next summer, Mamardashvili is ready to step in.

Football Insider revealed in September that Mamardashvili is pushing for more regular game time at Liverpool and believes he can become their number-one goalkeeper.

Doubts about Alisson's future, with clubs across world football looking to lure him away on a free transfer next summer, could provide the ideal opportunity for him to step up.

While Liverpool are expected to scour the market for a new goalkeeper, they may have the ideal replacement already waiting in the wings.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "You've got to remember Liverpool have still got Giorgi Mamardashvili who has been playing backup to Alisson.

"He will back himself to become Liverpool's new number-one if Alisson is to leave upon the expiry of his contract next summer.

"He has done well in cup games so far this season when he has been given a chance by Andoni Iraola, and they have also signed the young Belgian keeper Lucca Brughmans.

"He might not be ready to challenge for the number one shirt because he's still quite young, so that does leave the door open for Mamardashvili."

Meanwhile, Football Insider senior correspondent Callum O'Connell shared: "Mamardashvili came to Liverpool probably with the expectation that Allison would be leaving in the near future.

"It's easy to forget he is still an option for them, and maybe things haven't quite worked out for him so far. It'll be interesting to see if he does step up if Alisson does leave."

While there is optimism that Mamardashvili could step up and become the new first-choice goalkeeper at Anfield, the Reds are keen to assess a number of options.

Liverpool may well be tempted to enter the transfer market in search of a top-level replacement for Alisson, given how important he has been to their long-term success.

Football Insider revealed on 7 November that Liverpool have now set their sights on Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen, who could be the ideal replacement.

The 24-year-old has enjoyed an outstanding campaign with Brighton since the season began, and has kept 11 clean sheets in 14 appearances across all competitions so far.

Those performances have attracted interest from a number of Europe's biggest clubs, who are now believed to be keeping a close eye on the Netherlands international.

#2004. SPFL round-up: Partick Thistle go top as Hamilton stunned by Cove Rangers

Partick Thistle climbed to the top of the William Hill Championship with a 1-0 victory over rock-bottom Queen’s Park.

The moment of the game came 10 minutes after the break when Seb Drozd’s effort deflected to Tony Watt at the far post who headed Thistle to victory and climbed above Raith who drew 0-0 with Dunfermline.

Dylan Borso scored four times as they came from behind to win 4-3 and inflict a fourth straight defeat on Stenhousemuir despite playing more than an hour with a man less after Calvin Okike was sent off for the hosts.

Arbroath ended a run of five-straight defeats in style as they earned a convincing 4-1 win over Ayr courtesy of goals from Thomas O’Brien, Michael McKenna, Gavin Reilly and Jacob MacIntyre.

Cristian Montano’s equaliser cancelled out Alfie Stewart’s opener as Livingston drew 1-1 with Inverness.

In League One, Ross County moved five points clear at the top of the league after they ran out 4-1 winners over Peterhead.

Brian Graham and Chris Hamilton gave County a 2-0 lead before Mitch Megginson pulled a goal back for the visitors but the home side finished the job with further goals from Richard Chin and Kieran Phillips’ penalty.

Second-placed Hamilton suffered a shock first defeat of the season after they were thrashed 4-0 by rock-bottom Cove Rangers thanks to Edimond Oppong’s hat-trick and Joseph Teasdale’s late strike.

Goals from Jamie Hamilton and Cameron Elliott’s penalty helped East Kilbride come from behind and earn a first win four games with a 2-1 victory over Queen of the South.

Cammie Ross struck four minutes from time to give East Fife a second-straight win as they beat Montrose 2-1 who had goalscorer Blair Lyons sent off late.

Airdrieonians ended a run of three consecutive defeats with a 3-2 win over lowly Alloa courtesy of Rangers loanee Josh Gentles’ late goal.

Stranraer remained at the top of League Two with a 3-0 victory over Stirling who saw their five-match league unbeaten run come to an end.

Second-placed Clyde picked up a third win from their last four after they twice came from behind to beat The Spartans 3-2.

Leighton McIntosh and Scott Honeyman gave Dumbarton a first win in four with a 2-0 victory over Elgin.

Jack Brydon’s late strike earned Kelty Hearts a 2-1 win over Annan Athletic while Forfar drew 1-1 with Edinburgh.

Three defeats in four games for Milan in the Europa League. This was truly a poor performance and Ferencvaros definitely deserved to take home the three points. More than individual struggles, this was a tactical failure.

Great chance for the Englishman and the shot isn’t too bad either, but the goalkeeper makes a nice save with his left leg.

Quick counter-attack as De Winter’s clearance falls perfectly for the away side, allowing them to play their man in behind.

Terracciano finds Ramos in the box, who heads it down to Cisse, but the shot is not on target. Tough on the volley.

Really strange defending from Bartesaghi, trying to shield the ball and then losing out completely. Milan have zero rhythm in their build-up phase.

#1999. Wolves loanee has no regrets about rocky Celtic ride as he steps out of shadows to embrace the spotlight

Sam Johnstone has experienced enough of football's highs and lows to understand that joining Celtic was never likely to be a straightforward undertaking.

But despite a turbulent introduction to life in Glasgow, the Wolves loanee insists he has absolutely no regrets about taking on one of the most demanding challenges of his career to date.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The former England international headed north of the border earlier this summer in search of regular first-team football and a fresh challenge. What followed has been a mixed introduction, with inconsistent results bringing added scrutiny, while adapting to a new team environment has required patience.

His career has been defined as much by patience as it has by perseverance. The Manchester United youth product has spent lengthy spells waiting in the wings for his opportunity, often occupying a back-up or third-choice role, while striving to establish himself as a No.1

Arriving at Celtic has offered a welcome change of circumstances. Rather than being confined to a supporting role, Johnstone has the chance to make the position between the sticks his own as he continues to enjoy a sustained run of games and remind people of the qualities that once earned him international recognition.

There is also the matter of developing relationships with the defenders in front of him. Communication, trust and familiarity are essential for any goalkeeper, and Johnstone recognises that those connections take time to establish.

“I think I've got to get used to them, they've got to get used to me, and that only happens through playing and through games. It's great to be in the team,” he said. “To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm. It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.”

Having represented established clubs such as West Bromwich Albion and Crystal Palace, Johnstone is no stranger to pressure. However, he has discovered that the expectations at Celtic are particularly intense, arguably unlike anything he has experienced elsewhere in his career.

“Of course it has,” Johnstone admitted when asked whether fluctuating results had affected the mood within the dressing room. “I think the results affect it. This club's not used to losing, and we've probably lost too many games for this club.

“The expectation here, rightly so, is to win. Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation, and the lads know that. We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game. It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people, and honest with each other.”

Ultimately, though, signing for Celtic was an opportunity Johnstone was never likely to pass up. The quality within Martin O’Neill’s squad, coupled with the passion of the supporters and the chance to experience the club's unique atmosphere, made the move an attractive proposition.

“It's brilliant to play for this club,” he insisted. “The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training. When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here. It’s a great team to play in. The lads came up with the goods (on Thursday vs Besiktas], so we keep taking it game by game and go again on Sunday.”

Whether his time with the Scottish champions will provide the springboard to revitalise his career remains to be seen. Asked if the move had given him a fresh lease of life, Johnstone was typically measured in his response. “Let's see, let's see.”

#1996. Cisse says Milan ‘need to forget’ about derby win amid Europa League struggles

Alphadjo Cisse spoke to the media this evening and said that Milan need to forget about the derby win and build on the momentum with more wins.

The derby win certainly put Milan and the fans on cloud nine, especially since it wasn’t just a narrow 1-0 win. However, they now need to put some of that confidence to use in the Europa League as they only have three points after three games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ferencvaros are the opponents this evening, travelling to San Siro for the first time, and it could be a tough one as they are on nine points so far. Ruben Amorim clearly has faith in some of his deputies, though, with six changes made to the starting eleven.

Alphadjo Cisse is one of the players in the starting eleven and just a few minutes ago, he spoke to Sky Italia (via MilanNews) about the task at hand. He made it clear that Milan cannot keep thinking about the derby win, instead focusing on getting more wins.

“It’s important for me and the whole team. We always try to play to our full potential.”

“It was an important victory. But we need to forget about it and build on that momentum with a win. Getting the three points is important today.”

“I actually don’t know anything yet, the squad list hasn’t been released yet. I’d be very happy if the call were to come. But I’m thinking about today and tomorrow will be another day.”

#1994. After being benched for Celtic loan star, my on-field response was emphatic

Lucas Clearie has issued another reminder of his goalscoring potential after hitting a first-half hat-trick for Celtic B.

The 17-year-old was benched for the midweek KDM Evolution Trophy clash with Ross County, with Shim Mheuka preferred through the middle.

But Clearie responded in emphatic fashion just four days later with a first-half hat-trick against Beith Juniors. The striker opened the scoring in the 18th minute before adding another in the 42nd minute. He completed his hat-trick in the 45th minute.

His latest haul takes Clearie to an impressive 23 goals across Lowland League and KDM Evolution Trophy football this season.

Eighteen of those have arrived in the league, while he has also struck five times in four KDM Evolution Trophy outings. It was Clearie’s second hat-trick of the campaign after he previously scored three in a dramatic 4-3 victory over Stranraer.

Martin O’Neill answers Celtic ‘chucked it’ claims after major team gamble

The ongoing Celtic problem that must be ‘addressed’ in January

Chris Sutton delivers brutal ‘all-inclusive holiday’ jibe at new Celtic star

#1990. Rangers turn up heat on leaders Celtic despite controversy in Paisley

A bitterly cold, damp Saturday night in Paisley yielded precisely the sort of calculated, business-like victory that defines title credentials. Under the floodlights of the Marbill Coaches Stadium, Rangers maintained their pursuit of league leaders Celtic with a dominant 2-0 win over St Mirren.

In truth, the scoreline scarcely reflected the visitors’ control of proceedings, a superiority anchored by a dominant midfield display and punctuated by goals from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil in either half.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

This was an exercise in efficiency for Rangers manager Derek McInnes as his side arrived in Renfrewshire looking to maintain their unbeaten away record in the league this season. Making just one change from last weekend’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final triumph over Aberdeen, his side displayed a fluid composure that left the hosts chasing shadows for long periods.

Although Rangers have endured an inconsistent record on previous visits to Paisley, dropping points in three of their last four league outings, their latest success extended a domestic unbeaten run to 12 matches and left them in a confident place heading into the final international break of the year.

St Mirren, under the stewardship of Craig McLeish, had promised a robust, positive approach as they looked to arrest a worrying slide in form that had saw them lose six of their previous eight games. However, the reality for the Buddies was an evening spent largely in a low defensive block, starved of possession and unable to test Ivor Pandur in the visitors' goal until it was too late.

The breakthrough arrived in the 18th minute through a moment of controversy. Left-back James Penrice drove into the penalty area and went down under pressure from a trailing Samuel Ramos leg. While the home support vociferously claimed the new Scotland call-up went down theatrically, referee Nick Walsh pointed directly to the spot.

Naderi stepped forward, ignored the jeers, and showed admirable composure to confidently dispatch the penalty into the bottom right-hand corner, with Jacob Chapman diving the opposite direction. It marked the German’s sixth goal in his last seven games.

Going behind did little to alter St Mirren’s conservative shape as their build-up play lacked urgency, and Rangers continued to dictate the tempo. Their front three of Badredine Bouanani, Kim Minsu, and Kevin Kelsy probed intelligently. The hosts did have a penalty appeal of their own dismissed when Ramos’ header back across goal appeared to strike Naderi’s hand.

The second half followed an identical script, and the definitive blow arrived just after the hour mark. It was a goal engineered by the persistent work of Kelsy who battled fiercely to pick up Olwethu Makhanya’s pass.

His determination allowed the ball to break kindly to Neil, restored to the starting line-up, on the edge of the box and the midfielder side-footed effort took a wicked deflection of Declan John to completely wrong-foot the helpless Chapman, with the ball nestling in the bottom left-hand corner. It gave Rangers some welcome breathing room.

St Mirren did mount a late, spirited assault on the visitors goal, but were denied on several occasions by Pandur. Their best opportunity fell to substitute Eseosa Sule, who met a pinpoint cross from John at the back post. It seemed a certain goal, but the Croatian goalkeeper produced a sublime reaction save to preserve his clean sheet.

Ultimately, McInnes’s men navigated the closing stages with a minimum of fuss, starving the hosts of the ball and suffocating any remaining glimmers of a late comeback. The victory keeps them firmly within striking distance at the summit, a solitary point behind reigning champions Celtic with a game in hand still to play after this weekend.

#1986. Crawley Town to celebrate 130th anniversary with special edition shirt for Newport County game

To kick off the week, supporters will have the chance to purchase 1 of only 130 limited-edition shirts. The shirts will come in a commemorative box, along with a special 130th key ring and pin badge set, an anniversary scarf and commemorative certificate of authenticity. The shirt will be revealed on the morning of Monday, the 7th and will be released on sale shortly after, both in-store and online.

Each fan-edition shirt will have an embedded commemorative patch, making each shirt unique, as they will all have a different edition number between 1-130. More details on the sale process will be released in due course.

Following specialised social media coverage on Tuesday, the club will then celebrate the anniversary with an evening in the Innovation Group Executive Suite on Wednesday, December 9.

Tickets for the event will cost £30pp and include an inside look at the workings of the Broadfield Stadium, a curry meal service including poppadoms and sundries, and a look around a specially curated exhibition that captures parts of the club’s rich history. After the food service, the club will host a series of interview panels with former and current players from different eras, giving them a chance to tell their stories and chat about the best moments from their time at the club. Ticket sale proceeds from the evening will be donated to the club’s Community Foundation.

On Thursday, the club will host an online auction with various pieces of memorabilia on sale for supporters to buy.

Finally, on Saturday, the 12th December, the players will wear the commemorative shirts for the match against Newport County, with the matchday being themed around the 130-year celebration. More former players will be in attendance as the club’s guests of honour, and will be hosted in hospitality for the match before being paraded to fans at half-time. A special edition of Red Devils Diary will be produced, and further commemorative items will be available to purchase from the club shop! Following the fixture, the specially tagged ‘player edition’ shirts will then be added to the online auction for fans to purchase - of which the proceeds will, again,l go to the Community Foundation.

#1985. Amorim explains selection decisions including ‘strange’ Pavlovic absence in ‘crucial’ game

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has admitted that the match against Ferencvaros is ‘crucial’, but rotation was necessary.

With only three points on the board and five games left in the league phase, there is no more margin for error if Milan are to get themselves up the table towards top eight spots, which would secure automatic qualification for the last-16 and avoid a two-legged play-off.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, they face an opponent that have been in fine form, winning all three Europa League games so far, scoring nine and conceding only three. Their unbeaten run across all competitions has now stretched to 20 games, so they will be a tough proposition in front of 5,000 travelling fans.

Amorim spoke to Sky not long before the start of the game at San Siro, discussing his selections and the magnitude of the night in the Europa League context. His words are via MilanNews.

Can the post-derby enthusiasm boost the team?

“The feeling is positive. It’s important to work on the mental side. But then what matters is the next match: tonight is crucial for us. We have some players unavailable, but to be competitive in all competitions we have to show that all our players can perform. Tonight, there are three important points up for grabs.”

“It’s important. Mike isn’t there tonight, nor is Modric. We need his experience in case something bad happens. We need someone on the pitch who can provide security. Rotation is important to keep everyone fit, but it’s not rotation because it’s Ferencvaros we are playing. We want to win tonight.”

You have chosen to play Diawara alongside De Winter…

“It’s strange to start without Pavlovic. He and De Winter usually play together. It’s strange to start without him. But Diawara has shown he’s up to the task, both as a centre-back and wider. Koni is there to help him, even though Diawara doesn’t need anyone’s help.”

CR7 announced his retirement from the national team…

“It wasn’t the best way to end his national team career, but what he did for our country is clear for all to see. Everyone knows him around the world. Football is a window, many know Portugal because of CR7. He played with so many important players. He will give something to our country off the pitch too.”

#1982. Derek McInnes pinpoints Rangers biggest strength as St Mirren fume over penalty award and VAR consistency

Derek McInnes insists Rangers are heading in the right direction after extending their unbeaten domestic run to 12 matches with a comfortable 2-0 victory over St Mirren in Paisley.

Goals in either half from Ryan Naderi and captain Dan Neil secured another valuable three points for the Ibrox side, who moved to within a point of league leaders Celtic, with a game in hand still to play after this weekend.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Despite acknowledging that his team could have been more clinical in front of goal, McInnes was delighted with the way his players approached what he considers one of the more difficult away assignments in the Scottish Premiership.

“I think this is a hard place to come for any team, but for our club as well, over the years it's never easy and we didn't expect it to be anything other than that,” McInnes said. “But I thought we dealt with the game really well. I thought we were really competitive from the get-go, I thought we were tenacious, we were aggressive, we moved the ball right.

“We just came back to that last part of it not being clinical enough. Quite ironic, we scored two goals tonight from a penalty kick and a deflected shot at the edge of the box, given all the chances we had, but I actually thought in the main it was no more than we deserved.”

Naderi was once again central to Rangers' attacking efforts, taking his season's tally to nine goals and five assists after confidently dispatching his first-half spot-kick.

McInnes was particularly impressed by the striker's work rate and physical presence, believing the forward has taken significant strides in recent weeks as he looks to establish himself as a dependable option to lead the line.

“I think he's so willing. His first port of call was to make sure he's a handful to play against and I thought he was that,” McInnes stated. “He needs to build that reputation for being horrible to play against, but equally at a club like Rangers you're going to get judged on the goals.

“He's totally shown that he's somebody you can depend on, somebody that can be trusted, somebody that you can rely on to get goals as well as bring in good performances.”

McInnes was equally thrilled with goalkeeper Ivor Pandur, who produced several important saves to preserve Rangers' clean sheet as St Mirren threatened a comeback in the closing stages.

“I think he's been very clean, very controlled with what he does. His distribution is brilliant, he makes good decisions,” he said. “I think there's so much potential in Ivor. With a rotten goalie, you're not winning nothing. He is somebody who we really take a lot of comfort from.

“I've played with goalkeepers who were brilliant and I've played with some who weren't so good and you never ever felt comfortable. With him, we do. He's been a big part of the amount of clean sheets we've had. I thought we worked hard for a clean sheet tonight but there was a spell in the second half where the space got a wee bit bigger and St Mirren managed to get a few opportunities. Thankfully, you always feel he's got that save in him.”

St Mirren have one win from their last nine league games and boss Craig McLeish was left frustrated by the first-half penalty award, questioning the consistency of the decisions made by officials following Samuel Ramos’ challenge on James Penrice.

“My thoughts on the penalty... If that's the criteria for contact in the box, then fine,” he said. “But Kabs [Ismeal Kabia] gets wiped out in the second half after he puts a cross in. I don't even know if anyone looks at it.

“We get an apology after the game at Ibrox for a penalty that we should have got on Kabs again where there was a decent amount of contact on it. I get that if the ref gives it on the field, then it's maybe difficult for VAR to overturn it. I think if he doesn't give it there and then, I don't think VAR gets involved to give it.

“It's a difficult one and it's a frustrating one from our point of view, but there's also bits leading up to it getting to that situation that we need to deal with better. I need to be careful with what I'm saying. It's a frustrating one from our point of view.”

Asked whether he had spoken to Nick Walsh after the final whistle to seek clarification, McLeish replied bluntly: “No, there's no point.”

#1981. St Johnstone boss banishes Dundee demons with ‘bitter’ declaration

Simo Valakari was thrilled to give St Johnstone supporters a 2-1 victory over Dundee to celebrate after recent Perth struggles against their Tayside rivals.

Dundee won twice at McDiarmid Park in 2024-25, the season Saints were relegated, but a transformed team has returned to the top flight under Valakari.

They drew level on 17 points with Dundee in the William Hill Premiership thanks to a fourth win of the season. Valakari lapped up the success, with fans joyous at a first home victory over the Dark Blues since October 2021.

“We are a totally new team and it is not good to hold on to all those memories,” said Valakari. “Me as a manager, of course I remember. At Christmas-time we were 3-0 down after 20 minutes of the biggest game of the season.

“And of course I remember when their fans were on the pitch celebrating on the last day. But my players don’t have this baggage. We are creating new experiences together; this is our new adventure.

“If I carried everything that happened in the past with me, I would be a very bitter person! You need to let things go; that’s why we didn’t even bring it up.

“But all the players knew how much this game meant to our fans. We needed to perform, and we did. And to perform the way we did against a very good team made it a deserved win.”

Josh Campbell headed Saints in front after five minutes before substitute Joe Westley replied early in the second half following a mix-up between goalkeeper Ross Sinclair and Cheick Diabate. Kai Fotheringham, on his first Premiership start for Saints, netted a deflected winner in the 72nd minute.

“We were very good in the first half,” said Valakari. “They changed things at half-time. It took us a bit of time to adjust and we conceded a goal in that period.

“My team showed their character and personality again. We got control back and it got better and better from that.”

Dundee manager Steven Pressley conceded that his team failed to match much of their early-season form. He admitted St Johnstone were deserving winners over the course of the match.

“Over the course of the 90 minutes, St Johnstone were probably deserving of the victory,” he said. “We didn’t quite reach the heights and the standards that we’ve set.

“It’s not a criticism, it’s just these players continuously produced really high performances and have set some incredible standards. We were just a little bit below them on some of the things that we pride ourselves on.

“And, on the things we pride ourselves on, I thought St Johnstone were very strong. We’re disappointed to go into an international break on a defeat.”
